There are two types of rotation operations: Right Rotation (Clockwise) : If type = 1 , rotate the deque to the right. This means moving the last element to the front, and repeating the process k times. Left Rotation (Anti-Clockwise) : If type = 2 , rotate the deque to the left. This means moving the first element to the back, and repeating the process k times.

title: Unordered Set Swap Function
description: You are given 2 sets . You need to swap these with each other.

title: Unordered Set Find Duplicate
description: You are given an array arr[] . You need to find the duplicates in that array and print them using an iterator. Note: Use unordered set, and give extra line after printing.

title: Vector Shrink To Fit
description: Given a vector and an integer newsize , find the size using resize and shrink to fit functions. Input Format: The first line of input contains T denoting the number of test cases. The T test cases follow. Each test case contains 2 lines of input. The first line contains size , the initial size of the vector, the second line contains newsize , the new size of the vector. Output Format: For each test case, print the size of the vector using resize and shrink to fit functions. Task: Since this is a function problem, you don't need to take any input. Just complete the function ShrinkMe that takes the vector and newsize and prints both the size. Constraints: 1 <= T <= 100 1 <= size <= 100 1 <= newsize<= 100
constraints: 1 <= T <= 100 1 <= size <= 100 1 <= newsize<= 100 Example: Input: 1 20 10 Output: 20 10

title: Elements Less Than K
description: A vector arr[] and an element k are given to you. You need to return a of elements less than k. The order of elements should be the same as that in the original array. Note: In case, there is no element less than k then return an empty vector. Example :

title: Vertical Sum in a Jagged 2D Array
description: Given a jagged 2D array arr [][], where each row may contain a different number of elements, find the minimum sum among all columns.

title: Distinct Characters In Sorted Manner
description: Given a string s , return a string containing all distinct characters from s in non-decreasing order.

title: Range Sum Queries with Update
description: Given an integer array arr[] and a 2D array queries[][] . Each query is of one of the following two types: Type 1: [1, l, r] -> Return the sum of all elements in the range [l, r] (both inclusive). Type 2: [2, index, value] -> Update arr[index] to value. Return an array containing the answers to all Type 1 queries in the same order as they appear in queries[][]. Note: Use 0-based indexing.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, q ≤ 10 5 , where n is the size of the array 1 ≤ arr[i], value ≤ 10 4 0 ≤ l ≤ r < n 0 ≤ index < n

title: Lucky Numbers
description: Given an integer n , determine if it is a Lucky Number . Lucky numbers are identified using a elimination process on the infinite sequence of natural numbers (1, 2, 3, 4, ...): 1. Remove every 2nd number from the sequence. 2. From the remaining sequence, remove every 3rd number. 3. From the remaining sequence, remove every 4th number, and so on... This continues indefinitely. Return true if n survives the elimination process (is a lucky number). Otherwise, return false . Examples :

title: Prime at Prime Index
description: Given an array arr[] of positive numbers, return the array containing index of prime numbers that are at prime index (1-indexing) .

title: Range Min Max Queries
description: You are given an array of integers of size N and Q queries. Your task is to complete the following functions: getMinMax(L,R): return the minimum and maximum in the given range [L,R] updateValue(index,value): update arr[index] to value. Note: 0-based indexing is used.
constraints: 1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 10 5 0 ≤ L ≤ R, index < N 1 ≤ arr[i], value ≤ 10 5

title: Longest Correct Bracket Subsequence
description: Given a bracket sequence s consisting only of the characters '(' and ')', and a 2D array queries[][] of size q , where each query is represented as [l, r] (0 based indexing), find the length of the longest correct bracket subsequence that can be formed from the substring s[l...r] (both indices inclusive). Return an array where each element represents the answer for the corresponding query. Note: Use 0-based indexing. A correct bracket sequence is a sequence in which every opening bracket '(' has a corresponding closing bracket ')' in the correct order.

title: Maximum Among Left
description: Given an array arr[] , find all indices i such that arr[i] is strictly greater than every element that appears before it in the array. Return the indices in increasing order . Example :

title: Range GCD Queries
description: Given an integer array arr[] and a 2D array queries[][] containing q queries, where each query is one of the following two types: Type 1: [0, l, r] -> Return the GCD of all elements in the range [l, r] (both inclusive). Type 2: [1, index, value] -> Update arr[index] to value. Return an array containing the answers to all Type 1 queries in the order they appear in queries[][]. Note: Use 0-based indexing.
constraints: 1 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ q ≤ 10 5 0 ≤ l, r, index ≤ arr.size()-1 1 ≤ arr[i], value ≤ 10 5

title: Range LCM Queries
description: Given an array arr[] and a list of queries queries[][] . Each query can be one of the following two types: Update Query: [1, index, value] --> Update the element at position index in the array to the given value. Range Query: [2, L, R] --> Compute and return the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of all elements in the subarray from index L to R (inclusive). Process all queries sequentially and return a list containing the results of all Type 2 queries. Note: All operations follow 0-based indexing. Examples :
constraints: 1 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 10 4 1 ≤ queries.size() ≤ 10 5 0 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ arr.size() - 1 0 ≤ index ≤ arr.size() - 1 1 ≤ arr[i], value ≤ 10 4

title: First Repeating Element
description: Given an array arr[], find the first repeating element index. The element should occur more than once and the index of its first occurrence should be the smallest. Note:- The position you return should be according to 1-based indexing.

title: Minimum Distance on a Grid
description: Given a starting point (sx, sy) and a destination point (dx, dy) on a special grid. From any point (x, y), you may move only right to (x + 1, y) or up to (x, y + 1) , and each move costs 1 unit of distance. Find the minimum distance required to reach (dx, dy) from (sx, sy). If it is impossible to reach the destination using only right or up moves, return -1 .

title: Sort according to an Array
description: Given two integer arrays a1[] and a2[] . Sort the first array a1[] such that all the relative positions of the elements in the first array are the same as the elements in the second array a2[] . Note : If elements are repeated in the second array, consider their first occurance only. Elements not in a2[] should appear in a1[] at the end in ascending order. Examples :

title: Allocate Minimum Pages
description: Given an array arr[] of integers, where each element arr[i] represents the number of pages in the i-th book. You also have an integer k representing the number of students. The task is to allocate books to each student such that: Each student receives atleast one book. Each student is assigned a contiguous sequence of books. No book is assigned to more than one student. All books must be allocated. The objective is to minimize the maximum number of pages assigned to any student. In other words, out of all possible allocations, find the arrangement where the student who receives the most pages still has the smallest possible maximum. If it is not possible to allocate books to all students, return -1 ;

title: Shopkeeper Profit
description: Given an array arr[] , where arr[i] represents the price of the i-th product, calculate the total profit as follows: For each product, find the first product to its right whose price is greater than or equal to the current product's price. If such a product exists, the profit for the current product is the difference between their prices. Otherwise, the profit is equal to the current product's price. Return the total profit obtained by summing the profit for all products.

title: Union of Arrays with Duplicates
description: You are given two arrays a[] and b[] , return the Union of both the arrays in any order. The Union of two arrays is a collection of all distinct elements present in either of the arrays. If an element appears more than once in one or both arrays, it should be included only once in the result. Note: Elements of a[] and b[] are not necessarily distinct. Note that, You can return the Union in any order but the driver code will print the result in sorted order only.

title: Common Elements
description: Given two integer arrays a[] and b[] , return an array containing all elements common to both arrays in sorted order. If an element appears multiple times in both arrays, it should appear in the output as many times as it is common to both arrays.

title: Preorder to BST
description: Given an array pre[] representing the preorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree . Construct the corresponding BST and return its root . Note: All node values are distinct.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 3 , n is the size of pre 1 ≤ pre[i] ≤ 10 4

title: Keypad Typing
description: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters. Each letter corresponds to a number on a standard keypad, as shown in the figure. Replace every character in s with its corresponding keypad number and return the resulting numeric string.

title: Connected Groups of 1s
description: Given an n × m binary grid , count the number of connected groups formed by cells containing 1. Two cells belong to the same group if they are adjacent horizontally or vertically . Diagonal adjacency is not considered.

title: First Greater Element
description: Given an array arr[] of integers, for each element arr[i] , find the smallest element arr[j] such that j < i and arr[j] > arr[i] . If no such element exists, return -1 for that position.

title: Zero Sum Subarrays
description: You are given an array arr[] of integers. Find the total count of subarrays with their sum equal to 0.

title: Check Equal Arrays
description: Given two arrays a[] and b[] of equal size, the task is to find whether the elements in the arrays are equal. Two arrays are said to be equal if both contain the same set of elements, arrangements (or permutations) of elements may be different though. Note: If there are repetitions, then counts of repeated elements must also be the same for two arrays to be equal.

title: Check for Path in a 2D Grid with Obstacles
description: Given a grid mat[][] of size n × n containing integers 0 , 1 , 2 , and 3 having the following meanings 1 represents the source cell 2 represents the destination cell 3 represents a blank cell through which movement is allowed 0 represents a wall that cannot be traversed There is exactly one source and one destination in the grid. Find whether a path exists from the source cell to the destination cell. Movement is allowed in four directions: up, down, left, and right. Examples :

title: Removing Consecutive Elements
description: Given an array arr[] of positive elements and two special numbers x and y . Remove all consecutive same special numbers. The final array should be free from any consecutive same special elements. Note: The final array may be empty. Examples :

title: Minimum Cost Path with 4 Moves
description: Given a square grid of size n x b, each cell of which contains an integer cost that represents a cost to traverse through that cell, we need to find a path from the top left cell to the bottom right cell by which the total cost incurred is minimum. From the cell (i,j) we can go (i,j-1), (i, j+1), (i-1, j), (i+1, j). Examples :

title: Kth Smallest
description: Given an integer array arr[] and an integer k , find and return the k th smallest element in the given array. Note: The kth smallest element is determined based on the sorted order of the array. Examples :

title: Implement Trie
description: Implement the Trie class with the following functions: insert(word) : Inserts the string word into the trie. search(word) : Returns true if word exists in the trie; otherwise returns false. isPrefix(word) : Returns true if word is a prefix of at least one string stored in the trie; otherwise returns false. For input, the driver uses a 2D array query[][] , where each query is one of the following: Type 1: [1, word] -> Calls insert(word). Type 2: [2, word] -> Calls search(word) and stores the returned value. Type 3: [3, word] -> Calls isPrefix(word) and stores the returned value. The output consists of the results of all Type 2 and Type 3 queries in the order they are processed. Examples :

title: Nth Number with Prime Digits
description: Given a number n . You have to find the n th number whose each digit is a prime number i.e. 2, 3, 5, 7. In other words, you have to find n th number of this sequence: 2, 3, 5, 7, 22, 23 ,... and so on.

title: Shortest Common Supersequence
description: Given two strings s1 and s2 , find the length of the smallest string which has both s1 and s2 as its sub-sequences . Note: s1 and s2 can have both uppercase and lowercase English letters.

title: Nth Catalan Number
description: Given a number n, the task is to find the n th catalan number. Catalan Number for n is equal to the number of expressions containing n pairs of parenthesis that are correctly matched, i.e., for each of the n(' there exist n ')' on there right and vice versa. The first few Catalan numbers for n = 0, 1, 2, 3, … are 1, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, 429, 1430, 4862, …

title: Rotten Oranges
description: Given a matrix mat[][] , where each cell in the matrix can have values 0, 1 or 2 which has the following meaning: 0 : Empty cell 1 : Cell have fresh oranges 2 : Cell have rotten oranges D etermine t he minimum time required so that all the oranges become rotten. A rotten orange at index (i, j) can rot other fresh orange at indexes (i-1, j), (i+1, j), (i, j-1), (i, j+1) ( up , down , left and right ) in a unit time. Note : If it is impossible to rot every orange then simply return -1.

title: Min Steps by Knight
description: Given a square chessboard of size n × n , the initial position knightPos and target position targetPos of a Knight are given. Find the minimum number of moves required for the Knight to reach targetPos. A Knight moves in an L-shape, covering 2 cells in one direction and 1 cell perpendicular to it. From (x, y), it can move to: (x ± 2, y ± 1) and (x ± 1, y ± 2) This gives at most 8 possible moves: Note: The positions are given using 1-based indexing.
constraints: 1 <= n<= 1000 1 <= knightpos ≤ [x, y], targertpos[x, y] ≤ n

title: First n Fibonacci using Recursion
description: Given a number n , return an array containing the first n Fibonacci numbers. The first two Fibonacci numbers are 0 and 1. Each subsequent Fibonacci number is obtained by adding the previous two numbers.

title: Numbers Containing 1, 2 and 3
description: You are given an array arr[] of integers. Find all the numbers in the array whose digits consist only of [1, 2, 3]. The order of the numbers in the output array should be the same as their order in the input array. If there is no such element in arr[]. Return [-1].

title: Count Only Repeated
description: Given a sorted array arr[] of positive integers where the elements are consecutive , meaning the difference between adjacent distinct elements is exactly 1. In the array, exactly one element is repeated one or more times, while all other elements appear exactly once. Find and return the repeated element and the number of times it occurs in the array. If no element is repeated, return [-1, -1]. Examples :

title: Search Query for Strings
description: A Trie (Prefix Tree) is an efficient data structure used for storing and searching strings, especially when dealing with prefixes. You are given an array of strings arr[] of size n containing only lowercase English letters, and an array of query strings queries[] of size q . An empty TrieNode* root is provided as the root of the Trie. Insert all strings from arr[] into the Trie and, for each query string, check whether it exists in the Trie. For every query, return 1 if the string exists in arr[]; otherwise, return 0. Note: The required Trie functions are already implemented in the driver code. You only need to call them.

title: Assign Short Codes in Stream of Words
description: A railway department is renaming several cities, and the corresponding railway station codes must also be updated. Given an array cities[] containing the names of n cities in the order they are renamed. Generate the station code for each city according to the following rules: If a city appears for the first time, its station code should be the shortest prefix of its name that is not a prefix of any previously processed city. If the city has already appeared before, then no unique prefix can be assigned. Instead, its station code should be the complete city name, followed by a space and its occurrence count (including the current occurrence). Return an array containing the generated station codes for all the cities in the given order.

title: Longest Subarray of Evens and Odds
description: Given an array arr[], return the maximum possible length of a subarray such that its elements are arranged alternately either as even and odd or odd and even.

title: Shortest Transformation Length in a Word List
description: Given two distinct words s and e , and a list of unique words words[] , where all words have the same length, find the length of the shortest transformation sequences from start to end. A valid transformation sequence must satisfy the following conditions: Only one character can be changed in each transformation. Every transformed word must exist in words[], including e. All words consist only of lowercase English letters. s may or may not be present in words[] . Return the length of the shortest transformation sequence from s to e. If no such sequence exists, return 0 .
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 5 * 10 3 , where n is the length of words 1 ≤ m ≤ 10, where m is the length of words[i]

title: Max Pair Sum Less Than K
description: You are given an array arr of size n and an integer k . Your task is to find a pair of integers in the array such that it follows two conditions: The sum of the pair is the maximum possible but less than k. Out of all such pairs, choose the one with the maximum absolute difference between the two integers. If no such pair exists, return (-1, -1).

title: Count Subsequences of Type a^i b^j c^k
description: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters, count the number of subsequences that follow the pattern a^i b^j c^k - some number of a's, followed by some number of b's, followed by some number of c's, with i >= 1, j >= 1, k >= 1. Note: Two subsequences are considered different if the set of indices picked for them is different. Since the answer can be very large, return it modulo 10^9+7.

title: Missing in Array
description: You are given an array arr[] of size n - 1 that contains distinct integers in the range from 1 to n (inclusive). This array represents a permutation of the integers from 1 to n with one element missing . Your task is to identify and return the missing element .

title: Maximize The Cut Segments
description: Given an integer n denoting the Length of a line segment. You need to cut the line segment in such a way that the cut length of a line segment each time is either x , y or z . Here x, y, and z are integers. After performing all the cut operations, your total number of cut segments must be maximum. Return the maximum number of cut segments possible. Note : if no segment can be cut then return 0.

title: Container With Most Water
description: Given an array arr[] of non-negative integers, where each element arr[i] represents the height of the vertical lines, find the maximum amount of water that can be contained between any two lines, together with the x-axis. Note: In the case of a single vertical line it will not be able to hold water.

title: Arrange Anagrams Together
description: Given an array arr[] of strings, group all anagrams together. Two strings are anagrams if they contain the same characters with the same frequencies, possibly in a different order. Return a 2D array, where each inner array contains a group of anagrams. The relative order of strings within each group should be the same as their order in arr.

title: Product array puzzle
description: Given an array, arr[] c onstruct a product array, res[] where each element in res[i] is the product of all elements in arr[] except arr[i] . Return this resultant array, res[]. Note: Each element is res[] lies inside the 32-bit integer range.

title: Roman to Integer
description: Given a string s in Roman number format, your task is to convert it to an integer . Various symbols and their values are given below. Note: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1000
constraints: 1 ≤ roman number ≤ 3999 s[i] belongs to [I, V, X, L, C, D, M]

title: Median of 2 Sorted Arrays of Different Sizes
description: Given two sorted arrays a[] and b[] , find and return the median of the combined array after merging them into a single sorted array.
constraints: 1 ≤ a.size(), b.size() ≤ 10 6 1 ≤ a[i], b[i] ≤ 10 9 a.size() + b.size() > 0

title: Top K Frequent in Array
description: Given a non-empty integer array arr[]. Your task is to find and return the top k elements which have the highest frequency in the array. Note: If two numbers have the same frequency, the larger number should be given the higher priority.
constraints: 1 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ k ≤ no. of distinct elements

title: Radix Sort
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers, sort it in ascending order using the Radix Sort algorithm.

title: Closest Three Sum
description: Given an array, a rr[] of integers, and another number target , find three integers in the array such that their sum is closest to the target. Return the sum of the three integers. Note: If there are multiple solutions, return the maximum one. Examples :

title: Word Break
description: You are given a string s and a list dictionary[] of words. Your task is to determine whether the string s can be formed by concatenating one or more words from the dictionary[] . Note : From dictionary[] , any word can be taken any number of times and in any order. Examples :

title: Stock Buy and Sell – Multiple Transaction Allowed
description: Given an integer array prices[] , where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day. Each day you may decide to either buy or sell the stock at price[i] , you can even buy and sell the stock on the same day, return the maximum profit that you can get. Note : A stock can only be sold if it has been bought previously and multiple stocks cannot be held on any given day.

title: Generate Parentheses
description: Given a number n , return all the combinations of balanced parentheses of length n. Note: A sequence of parentheses is balanced if every opening bracket has a corresponding closing bracket in the correct order . For example, "(())", "()()", and "(()())" are balanced, whereas ")()(", "))((", and "()))" are not.

title: Delete Head of Linked List
description: Given a Linked List, delete the head of the Linked List and return the new head of the modified Linked List. Note: Set the original head to NULL.

title: Is Linked List Sorted
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, find whether the given linked list is sorted or not. Note: The sorting can either be non-increasing or non-decreasing.

title: Join Two Linked Lists
description: Given heads of two singly linked lists, head1 and head2 . Append the second list to the end of the first list . After performing this operation, return head of the new list .
constraints: 1 ≤ number of nodes  ≤ 10 5 1 ≤  value of nodes ≤ 10 5

title: Word Search
description: You are given a matrix mat[][] of size n*m containing english alphabets and a string word. Check if the word exists on the mat[][] or not. The word can be constructed by using letters from adjacent cells, either horizontally or vertically. The same cell cannot be used more than once. Examples :
constraints: 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 6 1 ≤ word.size() ≤ 15 mat[] and word contain bot lower case and uppercase English characters

title: Word Boggle
description: Given a string array dictionary[] of size n containing distinct words and a character matrix board[][] of size r × c , find all words from the dictionary that can be formed in the board. A word can be formed by starting from any cell and moving to any of its 8 adjacent cells (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). Each cell can be used at most once while forming a single word. Return all dictionary words that can be formed in the board. Note: The words in the output can be returned in any order. Examples :
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 15 1 ≤ r, c ≤ 50 1 ≤ |dictionary[i]| ≤ 60 Each dictionary[i] may contain both lowercase and uppercase English letters.

title: Length of Circular Linked List
description: Given a circular linked list of size n , find the length of the list (total number of nodes).

title: Doubly Linked List Tail Insert
description: Given a doubly linked list of size n, insert an element data after the tail. The driver code will print the LinkedList both forward and then backward to verify the result.

title: Delete Head of Doubly Linked List
description: Given the head of a doubly linked list, delete the head node and return the new head of the list. Examples :

description: Given n tasks numbered from 0 to n - 1 and a list of p prerequisite pairs pre[][] , where each pair [a, b] means that task b must be completed before task a , determine whether it is possible to complete all the tasks. Return true if all tasks can be finished; otherwise, return false .

title: Circular Doubly Linked List Traversal
description: Given a circular doubly linked list consisting of n elements, return the circular doubly linked list as an array. The driver code will print the list both forward and backward to verify the solution.

title: Burning Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree and a target node, determine the minimum time required to burn the entire tree if the target node is set on fire. In one second, the fire spreads from a node to its left child, right child, and parent. Note: The tree contains unique values. Examples :

title: Check for Doubly or Circular
description: Given head of a doubly linked list, check whether the linked list is circular or not. Note: A value k is internally used by the driver code to construct circular or normal doubly linked list. k = 0 creates a non-circular list, while k = 1 creates a circular list by connecting the last node to the head. It is not passed to the function.

title: Find Middle of Circular Doubly Linked List
description: Given the head of a circular doubly linked list of odd size , the task is to print the middle element. The tail of a circular doubly linked list is connected to head via its next pointer, and the previous pointer of head is connected to the tail.

title: 4 Sum - All Quadruples
description: Given an array arr[] of integers and another integer target . You have to find all unique quadruples from the given array whose sum is equal to the given target . Note: All the quadruples should be internally sorted, i.e for any quadruple [q1, q2, q3, q4] it should be : q1 ≤ q2 ≤ q3 ≤ q4. Examples :

title: Intersection of Arrays with Distinct
description: Given two unsorted integer arrays a[] and b[] each consisting of distinct elements, the task is to return the count of elements in the intersection (or common elements) of the two arrays. Intersection of two arrays can be defined as the set containing distinct common elements between the two arrays.

title: Excel Column Number from Name
description: Given a string s representing the column title of an Excel sheet, return its corresponding column number. In Excel, columns are labeled using uppercase English letters as follows: A → 1, B → 2, ..., Z → 26, AA → 27, AB → 28, ..., AZ → 52, BA → 53, ... The column titles follow a 1-indexed base-26 system, where the letters A–Z represent the values 1–26 respectively.

title: Sort 0s, 1s and 2s
description: Given an array arr[] containing only 0s, 1s, and 2s. Sort the array in ascending order. Note: You need to solve this problem without utilizing the built-in sort function.

title: Ways to Reach Origin
description: Geek is standing at a point (x, y) on a 2D grid and wants to reach the origin (0, 0). From any point, Geek can move in only two directions: left, from (x, y) to (x - 1, y), or down, from (x, y) to (x, y - 1). Find the total number of distinct paths for Geek to reach (0, 0) from (x, y). Since the answer can be very large, return it modulo 1000000007.

title: Count Pairs with Max Diff
description: Given an array arr[] of integers, count the number of distinct pairs {arr[i], arr[j]} such that 0 ≤ i, j < |arr| and i != j and their absolute difference is maximum.

title: Maximum of arr[j] – arr[i] + arr[l] – arr[k]
description: Given an array arr[] of integres. Find the maximum value of arr[j] – arr[i] + arr[l] – arr[k], such that i < j < k < l .

title: Unique Pair in Array
description: Given an array arr[] in which every element appears exactly twice except for two elements that appear only once, find those two unique elements and return them in sorted order.

title: Mean of Range in Array
description: Given an integer array arr[] and a 2D array queries[][] of size q . Each query queries[i] = [l, r] represents a subarray ranging from index l to r (inclusive). For every query, compute the mean (average) of the elements in the specified range, and return the floor value of that mean. Return an array where each element corresponds to the result of a query.
constraints: 1 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10 3 1 ≤ q ≤ 10 5 0 ≤ queries[i][0] ≤ queries[i][1] < arr.size()

title: Adding One to Array
description: Given a non-negative integer(without leading zeroes) represented as an array arr . Your task is to add 1 to the number (increment the number by 1). The digits are stored such that the most significant digit is at the starting index of the array.
constraints: 1 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 10 6 0 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 9 There are no leading zeros in the input number.

title: Subarrays with Same Min and Max
description: Given an array arr[] of integers, your task is to determine the number of subarrays where the minimum and maximum elements are equal.

title: Minimum Product of k Elements
description: Given an array arr of positive integers, return the minimum possible product of any k elements from the array. Return the result modulo 1e9 + 7 .

title: Max Value Permutation
description: Given an array arr[] of integers, rearrange its elements in any order to maximize the value of: Σ ( arr[i] × i ), where 0 ≤ i < n Return the maximum possible value .

title: K-th in a[] Missing from b[]
description: Given two integer arrays a[] and b[] , where a[] is sorted in strictly increasing order and b[] is an unsorted array, find the k-th element of a[] that is not present in b[]. If fewer than k such elements exist, return -1.

title: Number of Matches
description: There are n players participating in a knockout tournament. The rating of the i-th player is given by arr[i] , where all ratings are distinct. The tournament is conducted in rounds following these rules: The 1st player competes against the 2nd player, the 3rd player competes against the 4th player, and so on. In each match, the player with the higher rating wins and advances to the next round. If the number of players in a round is odd, the last player advances to the next round without playing a match. The tournament continues until only one player remains. For each player, find the number of matches won during the entire tournament.

title: Minimum Sum from Every Three Consecutive Elements
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers, find the minimum possible sum by repeatedly choosing one element from every group of three consecutive elements. After choosing an element at index i , the next choice must be made from the next three positions after i. Return the minimum sum required to cover the array using this rule. If the array size is less than 3, return 0.

title: Merge and Sort
description: Given two arrays arr1[] and arr2[] , return the merged array in ascending order containing unique elements.

title: Minimum Right Flips to Turn On All Bulbs
description: Given a binary array arr[] , where 0 represents a bulb that is off and 1 represents a bulb that is on , find the minimum number of switches required to turn on all the bulbs. Pressing the switch of the ith bulb toggles the state of that bulb and every bulb to its right.

title: Possible to Form a Regular Polygon
description: Given a binary array arr[] of size n , where the elements are placed at equal distances along the circumference of a circle, find if it is possible to form a regular polygon using only the positions where arr[i] = 1 as its vertices.

title: Missing And Repeating
description: Given an unsorted array arr[] of size n , containing elements from the range 1 to n , it is known that one number in this range is missing , and another number occurs twice in the array, find both the duplicate number and the missing number.

title: Palindrome Array
description: Given an array arr[] , the task is to find whether the arr is palindrome or not. An array is said to be palindrome if its reverse array matches the original array.

title: Subarrays with given sum
description: Given an unsorted array arr[] of integers and a sum k . Count the number of subarrays that add to a given number k.

title: Equal Sum with Insertion
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers. Find the smallest non-negative integer x that can be inserted between any two elements of the array such that the sum of the elements in the subarray before x is equal to the sum of the elements in the subarray after x, with x being included in either of the two subarrays. Return a list containing three integers: The smallest non-negative integer x that can be inserted. The position (1-indexed) where x is inserted. A flag indicating whether x was added to the first subarray (1) or the second subarray (2). Note: If the returned answer is correct, the driver code will print true, otherwise, it will print false.

title: Longest Subsequence with Adjacent Diff as 1
description: Given an array arr[] with n elements. find the longest subsequence such that the absolute difference between adjacent elements is one.

title: Cumulative Frequencies in an Array
description: Given an array arr[] of elements. The task is to calculate the cumulative frequency of each distinct element of the array. Note: Cumulative frequency should be taken according to the sorted order of array elements.

title: Minimum N-th Power More Than Array Product
description: Given an array arr[] of integers, find the minimum positive integer x such that when each element in the array is replaced by x, the product of the new array is strictly greater than the product of the original array.

title: Buildings with Sunlight
description: Given the array arr[] of heights of certain buildings that lie adjacent to each other, Sunlight starts falling from the left side of the buildings. If there is a building of a certain height, all the buildings to the right side of it having lesser heights cannot see the sun. Find the total number of buildings that receive sunlight. Note: Buildings with equal height do not block each other and can also receive sunlight.

title: Max Distance Between Two in Array
description: Given an unsorted array arr[] and two distinct elements x and y , find how many elements lie between them in the array, excluding x and y themselves. If either x or y appears multiple times in the array, consider the pair of occurrences that are farthest apart (i.e., have the maximum distance between their indices). If either of the given elements is not present in the array, return -1.

title: Max Sum Subarray of Non-Negative
description: Given an array of integers arr[] , find the contiguous subarray with the maximum sum that contains only non-negative numbers. If multiple subarrays have the same maximum sum return the one with longest length. If there is still a tie, return the subarray with the smallest starting index. If the array contains only negative numbers, return -1.

title: Kth Boom Number
description: A Boom number is a positive integer whose decimal representation consists only of the digits 2 and 3 . Given an integer k , return the kth smallest Boom number. Since the answer can be very large and may not fit in standard integer data types, return it as a string.

title: Check for Bitonic with Same Numbers
description: Given an array arr[] of non-negative integers, determine whether the array is perfect. An array is considered perfect if it first strictly increases, then remains constant, and finally strictly decreases. Any of these three parts can be empty.

title: First and Last in Unosrted
description: Given an unsorted array arr[] of integers and a key which is present in this array. Find the start index (index where the element is first found from left in the array) and end index (index where the element is first found from right in the array). Return an array of length 2 with elements start index and end index . Note: If the key does not exist in the array then return -1 for both start and end index.

title: Pascal Triangle
description: Given a positive integer n , return the n th row of pascal's triangle . Pascal's triangle is a triangular array of the binomial coefficients formed by summing up the elements of previous row.

title: Non-Repeating Element
description: Find the first non-repeating element in a given array arr of integers and if there is not present any non-repeating element then return 0 Note: The array consists of only positive and negative integers and not zero .

title: Earliest Last Occurrence
description: Given an integer array arr[], that may contain duplicate elements, find the element whose last occurrence appears first in the array. For every distinct element, determine the index of its last occurrence in the array. Return the element whose last occurrence has the smallest index.

title: Subarrays with Max in Range
description: Given an integer array arr[] and two integers l and r . Find the count of subarrays where the maximum element in that subarray is in range [l, r]. In other words, the max element is at least l and at most r. Examples :

title: Check Pairs of Equal Sum
description: Given an array arr . Find if there are two pairs (a, b) and (c, d) such that a+b = c+d.

title: Max value
description: In a given array arr[], find the maximum value of (arr[i] – i) - (arr[j] – j) where i is not equal to j and n is the size of the array. i and j vary from 0 to n-1 arr[] .

title: Flip to Maximize 1s
description: Given an array arr[] consisting of 0’s and 1’s . A flip operation involves changing all 0's to 1's and all 1's to 0's within a contiguous subarray. Formally, select a range (l, r) in the array arr[], such that (0 ≤ l ≤ r < n) holds and flip the elements in this range. Return the maximum number of 1's you can get in the array after doing at most 1 flip operation. Examples :

title: Sum of Subarrays
description: Given an array arr[] , find the sum of all the subarrays of the given array. Note: It is guaranteed that the total sum will fit within a 32-bit integer range.

title: Queries to Count Smaller or Equal in Other Array
description: Given two arrays a[] and b[] of size n , and an array query[] containing q queries. Each query x represents an index of array a . For each query, count the number of elements in b that are less than or equal to a[x] .

title: Maximum Gap
description: Given an array arr[] of positive elements. Your have to find the maximum difference between its two consecutive elements in its sorted form. Return 0 if the array contains less than 2 elements.

title: Find Kth Rotation
description: Given an increasing sorted rotated array arr[] of distinct integers. The array is right-rotated k times. Find the value of k . Let's suppose we have an array arr[] = [2, 4, 6, 9], if we rotate it by 2 times it will look like this: After 1st Rotation : [9, 2, 4, 6] After 2nd Rotation : [6, 9, 2, 4]

title: Closest in Sorted Array
description: Given a sorted array arr[] of positive integers. The task is to find the closest value in the array to the given number k . The array may contain duplicate values. Note : If the difference with k is the same for two values in the array return the greater value. Examples :

title: Count Pairs With Maximum Sum
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers, count the number of pairs (i, j) such that i < j and arr[i] + arr[j] is the maximum possible pair sum among all pairs. Return the count of all such pairs.

title: Remove Sandwiched Vowels
description: Given string s containing only lowercase English alphabets, eliminate the vowels from the string that occur between two consonants (sandwiched between two immediately adjacent consonants). Return the new string.

title: Top k Frequent in Stream
description: Given an array arr[] of integers and an integer k , traverse the array from left to right. After processing each element, find the k most frequent elements so far. For each step, form an array containing these elements sorted according to the following rules: Elements with higher frequency appear first. If two elements have the same frequency, the smaller element appears first. If the number of distinct elements encountered so far is less than k , include all of them. Return a 2D array where the i-th row contains the top frequent elements after processing arr[i].

title: Sort by Set Bit Count
description: Given an array arr[] of integers, sort the array (in descending order) according to count of set bits in binary representation of array elements. Note: For integers having same number of set bits in their binary representation, sort according to their position in the original array i.e., a stable sort.

title: Minimum Initial Energy to Cross
description: Given an array arr[] . The array represents checkpoints from one end to the other end of the street. Positive number at a checkpoint increases the energy and negative decrease. Find the minimum initial energy required to cross the street so that the energy level never becomes 0 or less than 0. Note: The value of the minimum initial energy required will be 1 to start.

title: Count Increasing Subsequences
description: Given an array arr[] consisting of digits (where each digit ranges from 0 to 9), the task is to count all possible subsequences within the array where each digit in the subsequence is strictly greater than the previous digit. The final count should be returned modulo 10 9 +7.

title: Check if all array elements are distinct
description: Given an array arr[] of size n , check whether all elements in the array are distinct or not. Return true if all elements are distinct, otherwise return false.

title: Left or Right Positioned Array
description: Given an array arr[] , find if it can be rearranged such that each element is equal to the number of elements to its left or the number of elements to its right.

title: Replace All with Min Value and Greater Product
description: Given an array, update all elements of the given array to some minimum value x, such that the product of all elements of this new array is strictly greater than the product of all elements of the initial array. Examples :

title: Factorial of Array under Modulo
description: You are given an array arr[] of integers of length n . You need to calculate factorial of each number. The answer can be very large, so print it modulo 10 9 + 7 .

title: Longest Span in two Binary Arrays
description: Given two binary arrays, a1[] and a2[] of equal length. Find the length of longest common span (i, j), where i<= j such that a1[i] + a1[i+1] + .... + a1[j] = a2[i] + a2[i+1] + ... + a2[j].

title: Max Consecutive 1's with K Flips
description: Given a binary array arr[] containing only 0s and 1s and an integer k , you are allowed to flip at most k 0s to 1s. Find the maximum number of consecutive 1's that can be obtained in the array after performing the operation at most k times.

title: Count Values with Equal Array Remainders
description: Given an integer array arr[] , count the number of positive integers k such that all elements of the array leave the same remainder when divided by k. If there are infinitely many such values of k, return -1 .

title: Search Pairs in a String
description: Given a string s and an array arr[][] of n character pairs, count the number of pairs for which both characters are present in the string s . A pair is counted only if both of its characters appear at least once in s . Return the total number of such pairs.
constraints: 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 10 6 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 6 The string s and the characters in each pair are either lowercase or uppercase alphabets.

title: Check k Sorted
description: Given an array of n distinct elements. Check whether the given array is a k-sorted array or not. A k-sorted array is an array where each element is at most k distance away from its target position in the sorted array. Examples

title: Balanced Floor and Ceil Distance
description: Given a sorted array arr[] and an integer x, find if the absolute difference between x and its floor is same as absolute difference between x and its ceil. The floor of x is the largest element in the array that is less than or equal to x, and the ceil of x is the smallest element in the array that is greater than or equal to x.

title: Maximize Sum After k Negations
description: Given an integer array arr[] and an integer k , perform exactly k operations on the array. In one operation, you can select any element and change its sign: Replace arr[i] with -arr[i]. The same element can be selected multiple times. Return the maximum possible sum of the array after exactly k operations.
constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 10 5 -10 4 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10 4 The element range ensures that the maximum possible array sum fits within a 32-bit signed integer.

title: Min Product Subset
description: Given an integer array arr[] , find the minimum possible product that can be obtained by multiplying the elements of any non-empty subset of the array.

title: Max Length Removal with 100
description: Given a binary string s containing only '0' and '1', you may repeatedly delete any occurrence of the substring " 100 ". Find the length of the longest contiguous substring that can be completely removed by applying this operation any number of times.

title: Adding Ones
description: Consider an array arr[] of size n, initially containing all zeros. You are also given an array updates[] of k positive integers. For each value j in updates[], add 1 to every element arr[i] whose index satisfies i ≥ j. The indices in updates[] are 1-based. Perform all the updates and modify arr[] accordingly.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, k ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ updates[i] ≤ n, for all i from 1 to k.

title: Max Sum Pairing with Diff Less than K
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers and a number k , Return maximum pair sum with the following conditions on the pairs. Pair difference should be less than k. Pairs should be disjoint. For example if indices (x, y) is a result pair, then neither x nor y should appear in any other result pair. If no valid pairs can be formed, return 0.

title: ArrayList insertion
description: Given an array arr[] containing integers. The task is to insert elements of given array to an ArrayList and return that ArrayList.

title: ArrayList Operations
description: In this question we will be implementing q number operations on ArrayList. There will be different type of queries. A query can be of five types: 1. a x (Adds an element x to the ArrayList A at the end) 2. b (Sorts the ArrayList A in ascending order) 3. c (Reverses the ArrayList A) 4. d (prints the size of the ArrayList) 5. e (Sorts the ArrayList A in descending order) 6. f (prints space separated values of the ArrayList)

title: ArrayList Iterate Front to Back
description: Iterators are used to iterate over Java Collections. Here we will learn to iterate over an ArrayList arr from begin to end.

title: Binary Search on ArrayList
description: Given a sorted integer arrayList and an integer element k . The task is to check if the element is present in the arrayList or not and return the index. Examples :

title: Sum of Middle of two sorted arrays
description: Given two sorted integer arrays arr1[] and arr2[] of the same size. Find the sum of the middle elements of two sorted arrays arr1 and arr2.

title: Pairs with Sum Less Than Product
description: Given an array arr[] of non-negative integers, count the number of unordered pairs (i, j) such that: arr[i] + arr[j] < arr[i] * arr[j] ( where 0 ≤ i < j < n).

title: Subarrays Covering All Distinct
description: You are given an integer array arr[] . Count the number of subarrays whose count of distinct is exactly the same as the count of distinct in the entire array.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 4 , where n is the size of array 1 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10 4

title: Pairs with Less Than K Diff
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers and an integer k , find the total number of pairs of elements that have an absolute difference strictly less than k. Note: Pair (i, j) is considered the same as (j, i).

title: Max Modulo Pair in an Array
description: Given an array arr[] of integers, the task is to find the maximum value of arr[i] % arr[j] for any pair of elements {arr[i], arr[j]} such that arr[i] ≥ arr[j] and 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n.

title: Equal Point in Sorted Array
description: Given a sorted array arr[] , find an index i such that: Number of elements smaller than arr[i] on the left side equals to the n umber of elements greater than arr[i] on the right side. Return the index i . If no such index exists, return -1 .

title: Max Sum Strictly Increasing Subarray
description: Given an array arr[] of size n containing positive integers, find the maximum sum of a strictly increasing subarray. Examples :

title: Common in 3 Sorted Arrays
description: Given three sorted arrays in non-decreasing order, return all common elements in non-decreasing order across these arrays. If there are no such elements return an empty array. Note: Ignore duplicates, include each common element only once in the output. Examples :

title: Subsets with given Max Diff
description: Given an integer array arr[] of size n and two integers k and d , find the number of distinct subsets of size k such that the difference between the maximum and minimum elements in each subset is at most d. Return the result modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Max and Min In ArrayList
description: Given an integer ArrayList arr[] , return the maximum and minimum elements in the ArrayList.

title: Single Among Doubles in a Sorted
description: Given a sorted array arr[] . Find the element that appears only once in the array. All other elements appear exactly twice .

title: Doubling the value
description: Given an array arr and an integer b , traverse the array (from the beginning) and if the element in array is b, double b and continue traversal. Find the value of b after the complete traversal. Examples :

title: Good Pairs
description: Given an array arr of n positive integers, count the number of good pairs (i , j ) such that: 1 ≤ i, j ≤ array size arr[i] < arr[j] Two pairs are considered different if they differ in at least one index. Since the answer can be very large, return it modulo 10^9+7. Examples :

title: Number and the Digit Sum
description: Given a positive value n , find the count of numbers smaller than or equal to n such that the difference between the number and the sum of its digits is greater than or equal to a given value k.

title: Consecutive 1's not allowed
description: Given a positive integer n , count all possible distinct binary strings of length n such that there are no consecutive 1’s . Examples :

title: Next Smallest Palindrome
description: Given a number, in the form of an array arr[] containing digits from 1 to 9 (inclusive). Find the next smallest palindrome strictly larger than the given number.

title: Count Pair Sum in 2 Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays a[] and b[] of distinct elements. Given a value x . The problem is to count all pairs from both arrays whose sum equals x. Note: The pair has an element from each array.

title: Ways to Split into 2 with Same XOR
description: Given an array arr[] of integers, the task is to count the number of ways to split given array elements into two non-empty subsets such that the XOR of elements of each group is equal. Each element should belong to exactly one subset. The answer could be very large so print it by doing modulo with 10 9 + 7. Subsets with the same elements but derived from different indices are different.

title: Count Occurences of Anagrams
description: Given a word pat and a text txt . Return the count of the occurrences of anagrams of the word in the text. Example 1:
constraints: 1 <= |pat| <= |txt| <= 10 5 Both strings contain lowercase English letters.

title: First with K Occurrences
description: Given an array arr[] representing user IDs in chronological order of their occurrences, and an integer k , find the first user whose ID occurs exactly k times in the array. If no such user exists, return -1 .

title: Count of Subarrays
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers and an integer k . The special value of each contiguous subarray of given array is the maximum element present in that subarray. Return the number of subarrays having special value strictly greater than k. Note : Since the answer can be very large, return it modulo 10 9 +7.

title: Count Prefix Maximums
description: Given an array arr of integers, find the number of elements such that all the elements before them are smaller. The first element is always counted since there are no elements before it. Examples :

title: Sorted and Rotated Minimum
description: A sorted array of distinct elements arr[] is rotated at some unknown point, the task is to find the minimum element in it.

title: Count Pairs with i * arr[i] > j * arr[j]
description: Given an array arr[] (0-based indexing) of n integers, count all pairs ( arr[i], arr[j] ) in it such that i * arr[i] > j * arr[j] and 0 ≤ i < j < n.

title: Maximum Neighbours In ArrayList
description: Given an integer ArrayList arr[], return the maximum for every adjacent pairs in the ArrayList.

title: PriorityQueue Insertion
description: Given an integer ArrayList arr[] , you need to insert the given elements into a PriorityQueue. Note: PriorityQueue in Java is implemented as a min heap.

title: Sum between k1'th and k2'th smallest
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers and two integers k1 and k2 , find the sum of all array elements whose values lie between the k1-th smallest and the k2-th smallest (both k1th and k2th smallest are not included) of the array. Examples :

title: Next greater number set digits
description: Given a number n, find the smallest number that has the same set of digits as n and is greater than n. If n is the greatest possible number with its set of digits, report it. Example 1:

title: PriorityQueue Insertion - 2
description: Given an integer ArrayList arr[] , you need to insert the given elements into a PriorityQueue such that they exist in a max-heap order. Note: PriorityQueue in Java is implemented as a min heap but here you need to customize it to a max-heap.

title: Search in a Row-Column Sorted
description: Given a 2D integer matrix mat[][] of size n x m , where every row and column is sorted in increasing order and a number x , return true if the element x is present in the matrix. Otherwise, return false .

title: Repeated Removal of Kth
description: Given two integers n and k , consider the integers from 1 to n. In each operation, keep every kth remaining integer and remove all others. Repeat this process until the number of remaining integers becomes less than k. Return the smallest integer among the remaining integers.

title: Pythagorean Triplet
description: Given an array arr[] , return true if there is a triplet (a, b, c) from the array (where a, b, and c are on different indexes) that satisfies a 2 + b 2 = c 2 , otherwise return false.

title: Move All Zeroes to End
description: You are given an array arr[] of non-negative integers. You have to move all the zeros in the array to the right end while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements. The operation must be performed in place , meaning you should not use extra space for another array.

title: String Duplicates Removal
description: Given a string s which may contain lowercase and uppercase characters. The task is to remove all duplicate characters from the string and find the resultant string. The order of remaining characters in the output should be same as in the original string.
constraints: 1 ≤ s.size() ≤ 10 6 String contains uppercase and lowercase English letters.

title: Equal Sum and Product Subarrays
description: Given an array of integers arr of some size, return the count of contiguous subarrays for which the sum and product of the elements are equal.

title: Smallest Diff Triplet in Three Arrays
description: Given three integer arrays a[], b[] and c[] of equal size n , find a triplet (one element from each array) that minimizes the difference between its maximum and minimum elements. If there is a tie, return the triplet with the smallest sum. The final triplet must be returned in descending order.
constraints: 1 ≤ a.size(), b.size(), c.size() ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ a[i], b[i], c[i] ≤ 10 5

title: Two Pairs with Same Product
description: Given an array arr[] of distinct positive integers, find if there exist two pairs of elements [a, b] and [ c, d] such that the product of the first pair is equal to the product of the second pair, i.e., a * b = c * d. All four elements a, b, c, and d must be distinct.

title: Pairs with Given Modulo Value
description: Given an array arr[] of distinct integers and an integer k, countpairs arr[i] and arr[j] (where i ≠ j) such that arr[i] % arr[j] = k.

title: Min Subsets with Consecutive Numbers
description: Given an array of distinct positive numbers, the task is to calculate the minimum number of subsets (or subsequences) from the array such that each subset contains consecutive numbers.

title: Painting the Fence
description: Given a fence with n posts and k colours, find out the number of ways of painting the fence so that not more than two consecutive posts have the same colours . Answers are guaranteed to be fit into a 32 bit integer.

title: Minimize the sum of product
description: Given two arrays a[] and b[] of size n containing positive integers. Rearrange the elements of both arrays so that the value of: a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + ... + a[n-1] * b[n-1] becomes minimum. Each element of a[] and b[] must be used exactly once.

title: Move all negative elements to end
description: Given an unsorted array arr[ ] having both negative and positive integers. Place all negative elements at the end of the array without changing the order of positive elements and negative elements. Note : Don't return any array, just in-place on the array.

title: Remove Consonants
description: Given a string s , remove all consonants and return the modified string containing only vowels. If the string does not contain any vowels, return an empty string.

title: Unusual String Sort
description: Given a string s consisting of uppercase and lowercase English letters, rearrange its characters according to the following rules: All uppercase letters must appear in sorted (ascending lexicographical) order among themselves. All lowercase letters must appear in sorted (ascending lexicographical) order among themselves. The output string should alternate between uppercase and lowercase letters whenever both are available. If one category (uppercase or lowercase) is exhausted before the other, append all remaining characters of the other category to the end of the string in sorted order. Return the resulting string.

title: Remove Two Consecutive Same
description: Tom is a string freak. He has got sequences of words arr[] to manipulate. If in a sequence, two same words come together then Tom destroys each other. Find the number of words left in the sequence after this pairwise destruction.

title: Pair Sum Closest to 0
description: Given an integer array of n elements. You need to find the maximum sum of two elements such that sum is closest to zero.

title: Chocolate Distribution Problem
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers, where each value represents the number of chocolates in a packet. Each packet can have a variable number of chocolates. There are m students, the task is to distribute chocolate packets among m students such that: Each student gets exactly one packet. The difference between maximum number of chocolates given to a student and minimum number is minimum and return that minimum possible difference.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Given an array arr[] of distinct elements, which was initially sorted in ascending order but then rotated at some unknown pivot, the task is to find the index of a target key . If the key is not present in the array, return -1 . Examples :

title: Smallest number with at least n trailing zeroes in factorial
description: Given an integer n , find the smallest positive integer x such that the factorial of x (i.e., x! ) contains at least n trailing zeroes .

title: Minimum Steps with p or q Moves
description: You are standing at the bottom of a staircase with exactly n stairs. You can take steps of size p or q at a time, calculate the minimum number of steps required to reach exactly the n-th stair using only these step sizes. You can take any combination of steps of size p and q to achieve this. If it is not possible to reach exactly n stairs using any combination of steps of size p and q, return -1 .

title: Minimum Distinct Ids
description: Given an array arr[ ] of item IDs, where each element represents the ID of an item, and an integer m , remove exactly m elements from the arr[ ] such that the number of distinct item IDs remaining is minimized . Return the minimum possible number of distinct item IDs left after removing exactly m elements. Examples :

title: Count pairs Sum in matrices
description: Given two matrices mat1[][] and mat2[][] of size n x n, where the elements in each matrix are arranged in strictly ascending order . Specifically, each row is sorted from left to right , and the last element of a row is smaller than the first element of the next row. You're given a target value x , your task is to find and count all pairs {a, b} such that a is from mat1 and b is from mat2 where the sum of a + b is equal to x .

title: Triplets Where One is Sum of Other Two
description: Given an array arr[] , count the number of distinct triplets (a, b, c) such that: a + b = c Each triplet is counted only once , regardless of the order of a and b.

title: Sum of Pairwise Bit Differences
description: Given an array integers arr[], containing n elements, find the sum of bit differences between all pairs of element in the array. Bit difference of a pair (x, y) is the count of different bits at the same positions in binary representations of x and y. Note : (x, y) and (y, x) are considered two separate pairs.

title: Balanced Array
description: Given an array arr[] of even size, find the minimum value that needs to be added to any one element so that the array becomes balanced. An array is considered balanced when the sum of elements in the left half is equal to the sum of elements in the right half. Examples :

title: Sort Two Parts  Sorted
description: Given an integer array where the two parts around a break point are individually sorted, merge them into a single sorted array. The break point can be anywhere in the array, including at the beginning or end.

title: Marks from Ranks
description: Consider an input where all marks obtained are divided into intervals of consecutive numbers represented as l[] and r[] where l[i] and r[i] represent the starting and ending marks (inclusive) of the i-th interval. The intervals are sorted in increasing order and do not overlap. The rank of a mark is defined by its position among all valid marks in increasing order, with the smallest mark assigned rank 1, the next smallest rank 2, and so on. Given an array rank[] . for each value in rank[], find the corresponding mark and return as an array.

title: Complete Binary Tree Traversal with Array Input
description: Given an integer array arr[] representing the nodes of a Complete Binary Tree in level order traversal, return the nodes at each level in sorted ascending order. For every level of the binary tree, sort the values present at that level independently and return the resulting levels as a 2D array, where the i-th row contains the sorted values of the i-th level.

title: TreeSet Operations
description: You are given an integer array arr[] . You need to insert the elements of arr into a TreeSet and display the results. Also, you need to erase a given element x from the TreeSet and print " erased x " if successfully erased, else print " not found ". Note: Don't add a new line in any function.

title: The Painter's Partition Problem-II

title: Longest Common Increasing Subsequence
description: Given two arrays, a[] and b[] , find the length of the longest common increasing subsequence(LCIS). Note: LCIS refers to a subsequence that is present in both arrays and strictly increases.

title: First Negative in Windows of Size K

title: Length of longest subarray

title: Multiply by 11

The input string num contains only digits and has no leading zeros, except when num is "0". Since the result may exceed the range of standard integer data types, return the product as a string.

title: Smallest Non-Zero Number

If x is less than or equal to the current array element, x is decreased by the difference between the array element and x.

title: Distance Travelled in a Permutation of 1 to n
description: You are given an array arr[] consisting of a permutation of the set {1, 2, 3, …, n} for some positive integer n. The task is to calculate the total distance you must travel starting from the position of 1 in the array, then moving to the position of 2, and so on, until you reach the position of n. When you travel from arr[i] to arr[j], the distance travelled is | i– j |.

title: Subarrays Having Even Sum

Return the minimum cost to equalize the heights of all the towers.

Find the number of palindromic strings whose length is less than or equal to n, such that: Every character in the string belongs to the given alphabet. No character appears more than twice in the string. Note: Since the answer can be very large, return it modulo 10^9+7 .

title: Min Sum Pair using Digits

title: Count Smaller in Array
description: Given an unsorted array arr[] . Find the count of elements less than or equal to the given element x .

description: Given an integer array arr[] and an integer x , determine whether there exist four distinct elements in the array whose sum is equal to x. Return true if such four elements exist. Otherwise, return false.

title: First and Second Smallests
description: Given an array, arr[] of integers, your task is to return the smallest and second smallest element in the array. If the smallest and second smallest do not exist, return -1.

Return the final string after applying all roll operations. Note: A roll operation affects the current state of the string, including all previous modifications.

A number x is considered missing if x is in the range [lower, upper] but not present in arr[]. title: Maximum Average Subarray
description: Given an array arr[] and a positive integer k , find the subarray of length k having the maximum average value. Return the starting index of that subarray. If multiple subarrays have the same maximum average, return the smallest starting index.

title: Minimize the Heights II
description: Given an array arr[] representing the heights of n towers and a positive integer k . For each tower, perform exactly one of the following operations exactly once: Increase its height by k, or Decrease its height by k. After performing the operation on every tower, the height of any tower must not become negative. Return the minimum possible difference between the heights of the tallest and the shortest towers after modifying all the towers. Note: A slight modification of the problem can be found here . title: Gift Distribution According to Preference
description: Given a 2D array arr[][] containing the preference lists of all students, where each row represents the preference list of a student in rank order. The first gift in each row is the student's highest preference. The students are considered in increasing order of rank. For each student, assign the first gift in their preference list that has not already been assigned to a student with a better rank. Return an array containing the gift assigned to each student in increasing order of rank.

title: Sort Strings Ignoring Case
description: Given a string array arr[] , sort the array lexicographically while ignoring the case.

The capacities of the vessels are given in an array arr[] . The goal is to fill the container without any overflow, and no vessel can be filled partially. Determine if Charul can fill the container up to exactly k liters using the given vessels. You can assume there is an unlimited supply of water, but each vessel's capacity must be used fully.

title: Maximum Partitions to Make a Permutation Sorted
description: Given an array arr[] of size n containing a permutation of integers from 0 to n - 1 . Divide the array into contiguous partitions such that after sorting each partition individually and concatenating them in the original order, the entire array becomes sorted. Return the maximum number of partitions that can be formed.

title: Split Array Elements into Bounded Parts
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers and an integer k , split each element into the minimum number of parts such that every part is less than or equal to k , and find the total number of parts formed from all elements of the array.

title: Leading Digit and Exponent of Factorial
description: Given an integer n, let n! denote its factorial. Return an array containing: The first digit d of n!, and The exponent p such that 10^p (10 raised to power p) is the largest number that does not exceed n!.

title: Search in a K-Step Array
description: Given a step array arr[], a step value k, and an integer x, find the first index of x in the array. If x is not present, return -1. Note: A K-Step array is an array where the absolute difference between any two adjacent elements is at most k. For example, arr[]= [4, 6, 7, 9] with k= 2 is a step array because the difference between consecutive elements is ≤ 2. Examples :

title: Surpasser Count
description: Given an array arr[] containing distinct integers, find the number of surpassers for each of its elements. An element y is said to be the surpasser of element x if it is a greater element on the right of x. ie., if x = arr[i] and y = arr[j], i<j and arr[i] < arr[j].

title: Left Out Candies
description: Given n students sitting in a circle, distribute m candies among them. The i th student can only accept exactly i candies - if the i th student cannot be given the required i candies, they take none. Starting from the first student and moving around the circle, keep distributing candies in this manner until you cannot give the required amount to the next student. Find the number of candies left at the end.

title: Minimum to Add for Prime Array Sum
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers, find the minimum non-negative integer that must be added to the array such that the sum of all elements becomes a prime number.

title: Min and Max in Array
description: Given an array arr[] . Your task is to find the minimum and maximum elements in the array.

title: Rubik's Cube
description: Given a Rubik's Cube configuration in the string array present[] and n moves in the string array move[] , apply all the moves in the given order and return the final cube configuration. present[]: A string array of size 6 representing the current cube configuration. The six strings represent the faces in the following fixed order: UP, FRONT, LEFT, RIGHT, BACK, DOWN Each string contains exactly 9 characters representing the 3 × 3 stickers of that face. The center sticker of each face remains unchanged throughout all the moves. move[]: A string array containing the moves to be performed on the cube. n: The number of moves to perform. Apply the first n moves from move[]. The faces have the following colors: UP -> Yellow FRONT -> Orange LEFT -> Green RIGHT -> Blue BACK -> Red DOWN -> White Each move rotates the corresponding face by 90 degrees. U, F, L, R, B, D → Clockwise rotation. Ui, Fi, Li, Ri, Bi, Di → Anti-clockwise rotation. For example, R rotates the RIGHT face 90 degrees clockwise, while Ri rotates it 90 degrees anti-clockwise. Return an array of strings containing the final configuration of the Rubik's Cube after applying all n moves. The returned array must contain exactly 6 strings in the order UP, FRONT, LEFT, RIGHT, BACK, DOWN. The initial configuration and the arrangement of the six faces are shown in the image below.

title: First and Last in Sorted

title: Sorting All Except One
description: Given an array arr[] and an integer k , sort the array in ascending order while keeping the element at index k fixed at its original position. Return the resulting array.

title: Rearrange to Maximize Alternate Addition Subtraction
description: Given an array arr[] , rearrange its elements to maximize the the final value obtained with the following operations starting with value 0. Values at even indexes are added. Values at odd indexes are subtracted. Return the rearranged array that maximizes the final floor after all elements have been processed. title: Delete Smaller Than Next
description: Given an array arr[] and a number k . Delete k elements that are smaller than the next element (i.e., we delete arr[i] if arr[i] < arr[i+1]) or become smaller than the next because the next element is deleted.

title: Min Decrement by K Operations to Limit Array
description: You are given an array arr[] and an integer k . In one operation you can choose any element of array and decrease its value by k. Find the minimum number of operation such that all the elements in the array becomes less or equal to k .

title: Chocolate Station

In the move from i to i + 1 , the number of chocolates adjust by arr[i] - arr[i + 1] . A positive value means gains, while a negative value means loses. Geek can move to the next station only if the number of chocolates he currently has is non-negative. Initially, he has 0 chocolates, but he may buy any number before starting his journey. Each chocolate costs price dollors. Return the minimum cost required for Geek to reach station n .

title: Pattern Based Binary Palindrome Construction
description: Given two integers n and k , construct a palindrome of length n using a binary pattern of length k. The binary pattern must have length exactly k and start with 1. You may repeat this k-bit pattern as many times as needed to form a longer binary string. After forming the string, you are allowed to remove one or more trailing zeros from the end. Among all possible valid palindromes, choose the one with the maximum number of zeros Return a palindrome of length n that can be formed in this way. If no such palindrome exists, return -1 .
