This is a non-preemptive scheduling algorithm, so once a process starts executing, it runs until completion. Definitions: Completion Time (CT): Time at which a process finishes execution. Turnaround Time (TAT): Completion Time − Arrival Time Waiting Time (WT): Turnaround Time − Burst Time Return the average waiting time and average turnaround time as a list of two values.

title: Sort k Sorted DLL
description: Given a doubly linked list, each node is at most k-indices away from its target position. In other words, if a node is supposed to be at position i in sorted list, then it can be at any position from i - k to i + k. Sort the given doubly linked list. The distances can be assumed in either of the directions (left and right).
constraints: 1 ≤ number of nodes ≤ 10 5 0 ≤ k < number of nodes 0 ≤ node->data ≤ 10 9

title: Vertex Cover
description: Given an undirected graph with n vertices and m edges. Each edge connects two vertices. A vertex cover is a set of vertices such that for every edge, at least one of its two endpoints belongs to the set. Find the minimum number of vertices required to form a vertex cover.

title: Minimize Cash Flow
description: Given n friends and a 2D array transaction[][] , where transaction[i][j] denotes the amount of money that friend i owes to friend j . Design an algorithm by which the total cash flow among all the friends is minimized. Note: Please note there can be multiple solutions possible, and the solution will be judged according to its net flow, and if it correctly follows the cash flow. If, you're solution returns -1, this means the cash flow is not following the actual flow of cash.

title: Min Edge Reversals for Path
description: Given a directed graph with n nodes and m edges. A source node and a destination node are also given, find the minimum number of edge reversals required so that there exists at least one path from src to dst. If it is not possible, return -1.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ edges[i][0], edges[i][1] ≤ n 1 ≤ src, dst ≤ n

title: Partition into Two Halves with Minimum Sum Diff
description: Given an array arr[] of n integers, divide it into two subsets s1 and s2 such that the difference between the sums of the two subsets is minimized. Return the minimum possible difference. The sizes of the subsets must satisfy the following conditions: If n is even, both subsets must contain exactly n/2 elements. If n is odd , one subset must contain (n-1)/2 elements and the other must contain (n+1)/2 elements. The difference between two subsets is defined as abs(sum(s1) - sum(s2)). Examples :

title: Binary Tree from Bracket String
description: Given a string s representing a binary tree, construct the tree and return the root node. The string is formatted as follows: it contains an integer, followed by zero, one, or two pairs of parentheses. The integer represents the value of the current node. If no children, the integer is not followed by any parentheses. If two children, two pairs of parentheses follow - the first recursively represents the left, and the second recursively represents the right subtree. If only left child, then the next bracket has left subtree. If only right child, then there are two brackets, one empty bracket to represent a left child and next bracket has right subtree. Note: The driver code will print the inorder traversal of the constructed tree as the final output.

title: Minimum Cost Edge Tour
description: Given an integer n representing the number of vertices in an undirected weighted graph and an array edges[][] of size m, where edges[i] = [u, v, w] represents an edge between vertices u and v with weight w. Find the minimum cost of a closed walk that starts and ends at the same vertex and visits every edge at least once. Return -1 if it is not possible to visit every edge in a single closed walk.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 15 1 ≤ m ≤ 105 1 ≤ edges[i][0], edges[i][1] ≤ n 1 ≤ edges[i][2] ≤ 25 edges[i][0] ≠ edges[i][1]

title: Check Level Anagrams in Binary Trees
description: Given the roots of two binary trees root1 and root2 , check whether the nodes at every corresponding level of the two trees are anagrams of each other. Two levels are considered anagrams if they contain the same node values with the same frequencies, irrespective of their order.

title: k Centers Problem
description: Given n cities numbered from 0 to n − 1 and an n × n distance matrix mat, where mat[i][j] represents the distance between city i and city j. Select k (k ≤ n) cities to place ATM servers such that the maximum distance from any city to its nearest ATM server is minimized. Return this minimum possible maximum distance.

title: Number of Distinct Islands
description: Given a grid grid[][] of size n × m , consisting of characters 'L' and 'W' , where 'L' represents Land and 'W' represents Water, find the number of distinct islands in the grid. An island is a group of one or more land cells connected horizontally or vertically. Two islands are considered distinct if their shapes are different. Two islands have the same shape if one can be translated to match the other exactly. Rotation and reflection are not allowed. Examples :
constraints: 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 500 grid[i][j] == L or grid[i][j] == W

title: Shortest Distance in a Binary Maze
description: Given a binary matrix mat[][] of size n × m containing values 0 and 1, and a source cell src[] and destination cell dest[] , find the minimum number of steps required to reach the destination cell from the source cell. From any cell, you can move to its adjacent cells in the up, down, left, and right directions. 1 represents a traversable cell. 0 represents a blocked cell that cannot be visited. If the destination cannot be reached from the source, return -1.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 500 grid[i][j] == 0 or grid[i][j] == 1 The source and destination cells are always inside the given matrix.

title: Minimum Multiplications to reach End
description: Given two integers, start and end , along with an array of integers arr[] . In one operation, you can multiply the current value by any element from arr[], and then take the result modulo 1000 to obtain a new value. Find the minimum steps in which end can be achieved starting from start . If it is not possible to reach end , then return -1 . Examples :

title: 1s Surrounded by 0s
description: Given an n × m binary matrix grid[][], find the total count of all cells containing 1 that are unable to move out of the grid through a path of adjacent 1s. Adjacency means you can only move in four directions: Up , Down , Left , and Righ t. Diagonal moves are not allowed. Assume that the space immediately outside the grid is an open path . Any 1 located directly on the outer boundary of the grid (first row, last row, first column, or last column) can immediately step out, and any 1 connected to it can follow and also step out of the grid.

title: Safe States
description: Given a directed graph with V vertices numbered from 0 to V-1 and E directed edges, represented as a 2D array edges[][] , where edges[i] = [u, v] represents a directed edge from vertex u to vertex v. A vertex with no outgoing edges is called a terminal node. A vertex is considered safe if every possible path starting from that vertex eventually reaches a terminal node. Return all the safe nodes of the graph.

title: Most Isolated City
description: There are n cities labeled from 0 to n - 1 and m bidirectional weighted edges connecting them. Given a 2D array edges[][] , where each edges[i] = [from i , to i, weight i] represents a bidirectional edge between cities from i and to i with weight weight i . Also given an integer dis . For each city, consider all other cities that are reachable through some path with a shortest path distance of at most dis. Return the city that can reach the fewest such cities. If multiple cities satisfy this condition, return the city with the greatest label. Examples

title: Number of Islands After K Operations
description: Given a grid of n rows and m columns. Initially, all cells of the grid contain 0, where 0 represents water. You are also given a 2D array operators[][] , where each operator contains two integers representing the row and column of a cell. Each operation converts the specified water cell into land by changing its value from 0 to 1. After each operation, find the number of islands present in the grid. An island is a group of one or more land cells (or 1s) that are connected through their top, bottom, left, or right sides. Cells connected only diagonally are not considered part of the same island. Return an array containing the number of islands after each operation.

title: Merging Details
description: Given a 2D list details[][] , where each details[i] represents the details of a student, the first element details[i][0] is the student's name and the remaining elements are email addresses. Two details belong to the same student if they have at least one common email address. Merge all details belonging to the same student. Two students may have the same name but different email addresses. If an email address appears in details with different names, merge those details using the name from the first detail in which that email appears. For each merged student, return the name followed by all their unique email addresses in sorted order. Return the merged details sorted lexicographically by student name. If two merged details have the same name, sort them lexicographically by their email lists.
constraints: 1 ≤ details.size() ≤ 1000 2 ≤ details[i].size() ≤ 10 1 ≤ details[i][j].size() ≤ 30 details[i][0] consists of English letters. details[i][j] (for j > 0) is a valid email.

title: Prefix Sum of Matrix (Or 2D Array)
description: Given an integer matrix mat[][] with n rows and m columns, and a 2D array queries[][] containing q queries, where each queries[i] is of the form [r1, c1, r2, c2]. For each query, find the sum of all elements in the rectangular submatrix whose: Top-left corner is (r1, c1). Bottom-right corner is (r2, c2). The row and column indices are 0-based, and both the top-left and bottom-right cells are included in the sum. Return an array containing the answer for each query in the same order as the queries.

title: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination
description: Given an undirected weighted graph with V vertices numbered from 0 to V-1 and E edges, represented as a 2D array edges[][] , where edges[i] = [u i , v i , time i ] means that there is an undirected edge between nodes u i and v i that takes time i minutes to reach. Return in how many ways you can travel from node 0 to node V - 1 in the shortest amount of time.
constraints: 1 ≤ V ≤ 200 V - 1 ≤ edges.size() ≤ V * (V - 1) / 2 0 ≤ u i , v i ≤ V - 1 1 ≤ time i ≤ 10 5 u i != v i

title: Maximum Score Using Neighbor Products
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers, repeatedly remove one element until the array becomes empty. The process of removal is as follows, When removing an element, add the product of the element and its current left and right neighbors to the score. If the element is at either end of the current array, assume its missing neighbor has value 1. After removing an element, the remaining elements become adjacent. Return the maximum possible score that can be obtained.

title: Diamond Shape Pattern
description: Given a number n , print a diamond-shaped star pattern with 2n rows, where the number of stars first increases and then decreases to form the diamond.

title: Path With Minimum Effort
description: You are given a 2D array mat[][] , of size n*m . Your task is to find the minimum possible path cost from the top-left cell (0, 0) to the bottom-right cell (n-1, m-1) by moving up, down, left, or right between adjacent cells. Note: The cost of a path is defined as the maximum absolute difference between the values of any two consecutive cells along that path.

title: Half Diamond Star Pattern
description: Given an integer n , print the Half Diamond Star Pattern using * characters as shown in the examples.

title: Shortest Path with at most k Nodes
description: Given a weighted directed graph of n vertices represented by a 2D array edges[][] , where each element edges[i] = {u, v, w} denotes a directed edge from vertex u to vertex v with cost w, and three integers src , dst , and k . Find the minimum cost to travel from src to dst using a path containing at most k nodes. If no such path exists, return -1. Note : The cost from city A to B may be different from the price from city B to A.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100 1 ≤ cost ≤ 10 4 0 ≤ src, dst, k < n

title: Maximum Connected with One Change
description: You are given a square binary grid. A grid is considered binary if every value in the grid is either 1 or 0. You can change at most one cell in the grid from 0 to 1 . You need to find the largest group of connected 1's . Two cells are said to be connected if both are adjacent(top, bottom, left, right) to each other and both have the same value. Examples :

title: Min Edge Movements to Connect a Graph
description: Given a graph with n vertices (0 to n-1) and m edges. You can remove one edge from anywhere and add that edge between any two vertices in one operation. Find the minimum number of operations required to connect the graph. If it is not possible to connect the graph, return -1.

title: Minimum Travel Time
description: Given an n × n integer matrix grid[][] , where grid[i][j] represents the height of the cell (i, j). Initially, you are at cell (0, 0) and the value of t is 0. Every second, the value of t increases by 1. At any time t, you can move from a cell to any of its 4-directionally adjacent cells if the heights of both cells are less than or equal to t . Movement between valid cells is instantaneous. Return the minimum value of t at which you can reach the cell (n - 1, n - 1).

title: Shortest Path in Unweighted Graph
description: Given an undirected graph with V vertices numbered from 0 to V-1 and E edges, where edges[i] = [u, v] denotes an undirected edge between vertex u and vertex v, given two vertices src and dest , find the length of the shortest path from src to dest. If there is no path between src and dest, return -1. Note: All edges have a unit weight of 1. Examples :

title: Maximum Stone Removal
description: Given an 2D array of non-negative integers stones[][] where stones[i] = [x i , y i ] represents the location of the ith stone on a 2D plane, the task is to return the maximum possible number of stones that you can remove. A stone can be removed if it shares either the same row or the same column as another stone that has not been removed. Note: Each coordinate point may have at most one stone.
constraints: 1 ≤ stones.size() ≤ 1000 0 ≤ x i , y i ≤ 10 4 No two stones are at same position.

title: Shortest Path in Directed Acyclic Graph
description: Given a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with V vertices numbered from 0 to V - 1 and E weighted directed edges represented by a 2D array edges[][] , where edges[i] = [u, v, wt] denotes a directed edge from vertex u to vertex v with weight wt, find the shortest distance from the source vertex 0 to every other vertex. Return an array of size V, where the i-th element represents the shortest distance from the source vertex 0 to vertex i. If a vertex is not reachable from the source, return -1 for that vertex. Examples :

title: Mirrored Bridge Pattern
description: Given an integer n, print the mirrored bridge pattern using * characters as shown in the examples.

title: Print n to 1 Without Loop
description: Print numbers from n to 1 (space separated) without the help of loops. Examples :

title: Print GFG n times
description: Given a positive number n , print the string " GFG " exactly n times separated by a single space.

title: First n Fibonacci using DP
description: You are given an integer n , return the fibonacci series till the nth(0-based indexing) term. Since the terms can become very large return the terms modulo 10 9 +7.

title: Maximum Frequency with K Increments
description: Given an integer array arr[] . In one operation, you can choose an index and increment its value by 1. Find the maximum possible frequency of an element in the array a fter performing at most k operations.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, k ≤ 10 5 where n is the size of the array arr. 1 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10 6

title: Number Bridge Pattern
description: Given an integer n , print a number bridge pattern where the ith row contains numbers from 1 to i in increasing order followed by numbers from i to 1 in decreasing order, properly spaced as shown in the output.

title: Concentric Square Pattern
description: Given a number n , print a concentric rectangular pattern of size (2*n - 1) with numbers decreasing towards the center and 1 at the center.

title: Largest odd number in string
description: Given a string s , representing a non-negative integer, return the largest-valued odd integer (as a string) that is a substring of the given string s. If no such odd-valued substring exists, return an empty string ("").
constraints: 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 2*10 5 where |s| denote the lengths of the string.

title: Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses
description: Given a valid arithmetic expression s consisting of digits, operators, and parentheses, determine the maximum nesting depth of the parentheses. The nesting depth is defined as the maximum number of opening parentheses '(' that are open simultaneously at any position while traversing the expression from left to right.
constraints: 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 100 s consists of digits 0-9 and characters ' + ' , ' - ' , ' * ' , ' / ' , ' ( ' , and ' ) '.

title: Majority Element - More Than n/3
description: Given an array arr [] consisting of n integers, find all the array elements which occurs more than floor(n/3) times. Return the resulting array in strictly increasing order. If no such elements exist, return an empty array.

title: Sum of Beauty of All Substrings
description: Given a string S , return the sum of beauty of all its substrings. The beauty of a string is defined as the difference in frequencies between the most frequent and least frequent characters. For example, the beauty of string "aaac" is 3 - 1 = 2. Example 1: Input: S = "aaac" Output: 3 Explanation: The substrings with non - zero beauty are ["aaac","aac"] where beauty of "aaac" is 2 and beauty of "aac" is 1. Example 2: Input: S = "geeksforgeeks" Output: 62 Explanation: There are 91 substrings of the given strings. Like, the beauty of substring "geek" is 1. In this way the sum of beauties of all substrings are 62. Your Task: You don't need to read input or print anything. Your task is to complete the function beautySum() which takes string S as input paramters and returns the sum of beauty of all its substrings. Expected Time Complexity: O(|S| 2 ) Expected Auxiliary Space: O(1)
constraints: 1 ≤ |S| ≤ 500 S only contains lower case alphabets.

title: Koko Eating Bananas
description: Koko is given an array arr[], where each element represents a pile of bananas. She has exactly k hours to eat all the bananas. Each hour, Koko can choose one pile and eat up to s bananas from it. If the pile has atleast s bananas, she eats exactly s bananas. If the pile has fewer than s bananas, she eats the entire pile in that hour. Koko can only eat from one pile per hour. Your task is to find the minimum value of s (bananas per hour) such that Koko can finish all the piles within k hours.

title: Search in Rotated Array 2
description: Given a sorted and rotated array arr[] and a target key . Check whether the key is present in the array or not. Note: The array may contains duplicate elements.

title: Count Good numbers
description: A digit string is good if the digits (0-indexed) at even indices are even and digits at odd indices are prime ( 2 , 3 , 5 or 7 ). For example, "4562" is good because the digits (4 and 6) at even positions are even and the digits (5 and 2) at odd positions are prime. However, "3245" is not good. Given an integer N , return the total number of good digit strings of length N. Since the answer may be too large, return it modulo 10 9 + 7 . Note : A digit string is a string consisting of digits 0 through 9 that may contain leading zeros. Example 1: Input: N = 1 Output: 5 Explanation: The good digit string of length of 1 are "0" , "2" , "4" ,"6" and "8". Example 2: Input: N = 3 Output: 100 Your Task: You don't need to read input or print anything. Your task is to complete the function countGoodNumbers() which takes an integer N as inputs returns the total number of good digit strings of length N . As this result can be very large return the result under modulo 10 9 +7. Expected Time Complexity: O(logN) Expected Auxiliary Space: O(1)

title: Longest Subarray with Atmost Two Distinct
description: Given an array arr[] consisting of positive integers, your task is to find the length of the longest subarray that contains at most two distinct integers.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description: Given a string s of length n consisting of uppercase English letters and an integer k , you are allowed to perform at most k operations. In each operation, y ou can change any character of the string to any other uppercase English letter. Determine the length of the longest substring that can be transformed into a string with all identical characters after performing at most k such operations.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, k ≤ 10 5 s consists of only uppercase English letters.

title: Count Subarrays with k Odds
description: You are given an array arr[] of positive integers and an integer k . You have to count the number of subarrays that contain exactly k odd numbers .

title: Count Substrings with a, b and c
description: Given a string s consisting only a, b, c. return the number of substrings containing at least one occurrence of all characters a, b, and c.
constraints: 3 ≤ s.length ≤ 5 x 10 4 s only contains a, b, c.

title: Binary subarray sum
description: Given a binary array arr[] and an integer target , return the number of non-empty subarrays with a sum equal to the target. A subarray is the contiguous part of the array.

title: All Divisors of a Number
description: Given an integer n, return all the divisors of n in the ascending order.

title: Sum of subarray minimums
description: Given an array a rr[] of positive integers, find the total sum of the minimum elements of every possible subarrays . Note: It is guaranteed that the total sum will fit within a 32-bit unsigned integer.

title: Frog Jump
description: Given an integer array height[] where height[i] represents the height of the i-th stair, a frog starts from the first stair and wants to reach the last stair. From any stair i, the frog has two options: it can either jump to the (i+1)th stair or the (i+2)th stair. The cost of a jump is the absolute difference in height between the two stairs. Determine the minimum total cost required for the frog to reach the last stair.

title: Opposite Sign Pair Reduction
description: Given an array arr[] , return the final array by repeatedly apply the following operation from left to right until no more valid operations can be performed. If two adjacent elements have opposite signs: If their absolute values are different, remove both elements and insert the one with the greater absolute value, preserving its sign. If their absolute values are equal, remove both elements without inserting any new element. Examples :

title: XOR of a Number Range
description: Given two integers l and r , find the XOR of elements of the range [l, r].

title: Minimal Cost of Jumps
description: Y ou are given an array arr[] of height of n stones and an integer k , where arr[i] represents the height of the i-th stone. You start at index 0 and want to reach the last stone (index n-1). From any index i, you can jump to any index j such that i < j ≤ i+k. The cost of jumping from stone i to stone j is abs (arr[i] − arr[j]). Find the minimum total cost required to reach the last stone.

title: Geek's Training
description: Geek is going for a training program for n days. He can perform any of these activities: Running , Fighting , and Learning Practice. Each activity has some point on each day. As Geek wants to improve all his skills, he can't do the same activity on two consecutive days. Given a 2D matrix mat[][], where mat[i][0], mat[i][1], and mat[i][2] represent the merit points for Running , Fighting , and Learning on the i-th day, determine the maximum total merit points Geek can achieve .

title: Sum of subarray ranges
description: Given an integer array arr[] , the range of a subarray is defined as the difference between the largest and smallest elements within that subarray. Your task is to return the sum of the ranges of all possible subarrays in the array. Note: It is guaranteed that the result will fit within a 32-bit integer.

title: Maximum point you can obtain from cards
description: You are given an integer array cardPoints[] , where each element represents the points associated with a card. The cards are arranged in a row. In one step, you can take one card either from the beginning or the end of the row. You must take exactly k cards. Your goal is to maximize the total score from the cards you take. Given the array cardPoints[] , and the integer k , return the maximum score you can obtain. Examples :

title: Subarrays with K Distinct Integers
description: You are given an array arr[] of positive integers and an integer k , find the number of subarrays in arr[] where the count of distinct integers is exactly k. Note: A subarray is a contiguous part of an array.
constraints: 1 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 10 4 1 ≤ k ≤ arr.size() 1≤ arr i ≤ arr.size()

title: Stock Buy and Sell – Max one Transaction Allowed
description: Given an array prices[] of non-negative integers, representing the prices of the stocks on different days. The task is to find the maximum profit possible by buying and selling the stocks on different days when at most one transaction is allowed. Here one transaction means 1 buy + 1 Sell. If it is not possible to make a profit then return 0 . Note: Stock must be bought before being sold.

title: Stock Buy and Sell with Cooldown
description: Given an array arr[] , where the ith element of arr[] represents the price of a stock on the ith day (all prices are non-negative integers). Find the maximum profit you can make by buying and selling stocks such that after selling a stock, you cannot buy again on the next day (i.e., there is a one-day cooldown).

title: Aggressive Cows
description: Given an integer array arr[] , which denotes the positions of stalls. All the positions are distinct. There are k aggressive cows. Assign the cows to the stalls such that the minimum distance between any two cows is maximized.

title: Smallest Divisor
description: Given an integer array arr[] and an integer k (where k ≥ arr.length ), find the smallest positive integer divisor such that the sum of the ceiling values of each element in arr[] divided by this divisor is less than or equal to k.

title: Distinct Subsets
description: You are given an array arr[] of positive integers (which may contain duplicates), your task is to find all the unique or distinct subsets of the array. Note: You can return the subsets in any order, the driver code will print them in sorted order.

title: Subsequence with Sum K
description: Given an array arr[] and target sum k , check if there exists a subsequence such that the sum of all elements in the subsequence equals to k.

title: Count Greater on Right Queries
description: Given an array arr[] and q queries, where each query contains an index indices[i]. For each query, determine the count of elements in arr[] that are strictly greater than arr[indices[i]] and occur to its right. Return the count for each query in the same order as the given queries. Examples :

title: Expression Add Operators
description: Given a string s that contains only digits (0-9) and an integer target , return all possible strings by inserting the binary operator ' + ' , ' - ' , and/or ' * ' between the digits of s such that the resultant expression evaluates to the target value. Note: Operands in the returned expressions should not contain leading zeros. For example, 2 + 03 is not allowed whereas 20 + 3 is fine. It is allowed to not insert any of the operators. Driver code will print the final list of strings in lexicographically smallest order.
constraints: 1 ≤ s.size() ≤ 9 s consists of only digits (0-9). -2 31 ≤ target ≤ 2 31 -1

title: Ugly Number II
description: Given an integer n , return the n th ugly number. An ugly number is a positive integer whose prime factors are limited to 2, 3 and 5.

title: Combination Sum Without Repetition
description: Given an array arr[] and a target , your task is to find all unique combinations in the array where the sum of the elements is equal to target. Each element in arr[] can be used at most once in the combination. Note: You can return your answer in any order, the driver code will print them in sorted order. Test cases are generated such that number of unique combination does not exceed 10 6 .

title: Outermost Parentheses of Primitives
description: A valid parenthesis string is called primitive if it cannot be split into two non-empty valid parentheses strings. Given a valid parentheses string s , remove the outermost parentheses from every primitive substring and return the resulting string.
constraints: 1 ≤ s.size() ≤ 10 5 s[i] is either '(' or ')' s is a valid parentheses string.

title: Shortest Path in an Undirected Graph
description: Given a weighted undirected graph with V vertices numbered from 1 to V and E edges, where edges[i] = [u, v, w] denotes an undirected edge between vertices u and v with weight w. We are also given two vertices src and dest , find the shortest path from src to dest. If multiple shortest paths exist with the same total weight, return the one whose sequence of vertices is lexicographically smallest. If no path exists between src and dest, return {-1}. Note: The graph contains no negative-weight edges. Examples :

title: Maximum Depth Of Binary Tree
description: Given a binary tree, find its maximum depth. A binary tree's maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node. Examples :

description: Given a string s representing a valid mathematical expression in prefix notation. The string consists of uppercase and lowercase English letters as operands, and the operators + , - , * , / , % , and ^ . Convert the given prefix expression into its equivalent fully parenthesized infix expression and return the resulting string. Examples :

title: Prefix to Postfix Conversion
description: You are given a string s that represents the prefix form of a valid mathematical expression. Convert it to its postfix form.

title: Minimum Operations to reach 1
description: Given a number n, find the minimum number of operations to reduce it to 1. In each operation, choose a number x such that 0 < x < n and n is exactly divisible by x, then reduce n to n - x.

title: Search in Linked List
description: Given a linked list with the head node and a key, the task is to check if the key is present in the linked list or not.

title: Minimum Cost to Merge Stones
description: Given an array stones[] , where the i th element represents the number of stones in the i th pile. In one move, you can merge exactly k consecutive piles into a single pile, and the cost of this move is equal to the total number of stones in these k piles. Determine the minimum total cost required to merge all the piles into one single pile. If it is not possible to merge all piles into one according to the given rules, return -1 .

title: Minimum Days to Make m Bouquets
description: In a row of flowers, each flower blooms on a specific day. Given an integer array arr[] , where arr[i] denotes the day on which the flower at position i blooms. To make a bouquet, you need to collect k adjacent flowers that have already bloomed. Each flower can be used in at most one bouquet. Find the minimum number of days required to make m bouquets. If it is impossible to do so, return -1 . Examples :

title: Remove duplicates from a sorted DLL
description: Given a doubly linked list of n nodes sorted by values, remove duplicate nodes present in the linked list.

title: Generate all binary strings
description: Given an integer n . You need to generate all the binary strings of n characters representing bits. Note: Return the strings in ascending order.

title: Minimize Max Distance of Adjacent Gas Stations
description: We have a horizontal number line. On that number line, we have gas stations at positions stations[0], stations[1], ..., stations[n-1]. Now, we add k more gas stations so that d , the maximum distance between adjacent gas stations is minimized. Find the smallest possible value of d. Find the answer exactly to 6 decimal places. Note : stations sorted is in a strictly increasing order.

title: Delete All Occurrences in DLL
description: Given the head of a doubly Linked List and a key x . Delete all occurrences of the given key x if it is present and return the new DLL.

title: Postfix to Prefix Conversion
description: You are given a string s that represents the postfix form of a valid mathematical expression. Convert it to its prefix form. Examples :

title: Postfix to Infix Conversion
description: Given a string s that represents the postfix form of a valid mathematical expression. Convert it to its infix form.

title: Task Scheduler
description: Given a character array tasks[] of size n , where each character represents a CPU task, and an integer k representing the cooldown period, find the minimum time units required to complete all tasks. Each task takes one unit of time. During each unit, the CPU can either execute one task or remain idle. Two identical tasks must be separated by at least k units of time. Return the minimum time required to finish all the tasks.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 4 0 ≤ k ≤ 100 tasks[i] is upper-case English letter.

title: LFU Cache
description: Design and implement an LFU (Least Frequently Used) cache. Here cap denotes the capacity of the cache and Q denotes the number of queries. Query can be of two types GET(x) and PUT(x, y). The LRU cache should support the following operations: LFUCache(cap) : initializes the cache with a given capacity. get(key) : returns the value associated with the key if it exists; otherwise, returns -1. put(key, value) : inserts or updates the key with value. If the cache has reached its capacity, the least frequently used (LFU) key should be removed. If there is a tie between keys with the same frequency, the least recently used (LRU) key among them should be removed.
constraints: 0 ≤ cap ≤ 1 0 4 0 ≤ key ≤ 1 0 5 0 ≤ value ≤ 1 0 6 Up to 2 × 1 0 5 calls will be made to get and put .

title: Divide into Consecutive Groups
description: Given an array arr[] representing the values of cards and an integer m , rearrange the cards into groups such that each group contains exactly m consecutive values.

title: Count Reverse Pairs
description: You are given an array arr[] of positive integers, find the count of reverse pairs . A pair of indices (i, j) is said to be a reverse pair if both the following conditions are met: 0 ≤ i < j < arr.size() arr[i] > 2 * arr[j] Examples :

title: Minimum Absolute Difference In BST
description: Given a binary search tree having n (n > 1) nodes, return the minimum absolute difference between any two nodes.

title: Buy Stock with Transaction Fee
description: You are given an array arr[] , in which arr[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day and an integer k represents a transaction fee . Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete as many transactions as you like, but you need to pay the transaction fee for each transaction. Note: You may not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously (i.e., you must sell the stock before you buy again).

title: Number of Longest Increasing Subsequence
description: Given an integer array arr , return the number of longest increasing subsequences. Note that the sequence has to be strictly increasing.

title: Assign Cookies
description: You are given an array greed[] , where greed[i] represents the minimum size of cookie required to satisfy the i-th child, and an array cookie[] , where cookie[j] represents the size of the j-th cookie. Each child can receive at most one cookie. A child i will be satisfied if they receive a cookie j such that cookie[j] >= greed[i] . Your task is to determine the maximum number of children that can be satisfied.

title: Bus Ticket Change
description: You are given an array arr[] representing passengers in a queue. Each bus ticket costs 5 coins , and arr[i] denotes the note a passenger uses to pay (which can be 5, 10, or 20 ). You must serve the passengers in the given order and always provide the correct change so that each passenger effectively pays exactly 5 coins . Your task is to determine whether it is possible to serve all passengers in the queue without ever running out of change.

title: Maximum Sum Combination
description: You are given two integer arrays a[] and b[] of equal size. A sum combination is formed by adding one element from a[] and one from b[] , using each index pair (i, j) at most once. Return the top k maximum sum combinations, sorted in non-increasing order.
constraints: 1 ≤ a.size() = b.size() ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ k ≤ a.size() 1 ≤ a[i], b[i] ≤ 10 4

title: Minimum Candy Distribution
description: There are n children standing in a line. Each child is assigned a rating value given in the integer array arr[] . You are giving candies to these children subjected to the following requirements: Each child must have at least one candy . Children with a higher rating than their neighbors get more candies than their neighbors. Return the minimum number of candies you need to have to distribute. Note: The answer will always fit into a 32-bit integer.

title: Non-Overlapping Intervals
description: Given a 2D array intervals[][] of size n, where intervals[i] = [start i , end i ]. Return the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest of the intervals non-overlapping. Note: Two intervals are considered non-overlapping if the end time of one interval is less than or equal to the start time of the next interval.

title: Minimum Window Subsequence
description: You are given two strings, s1 and s2 . Your task is to find the smallest substring in s1 such that s2 appears as a subsequence within that substring. The characters of s2 must appear in the same sequence within the substring of s1. If there are multiple valid substrings of the same minimum length, return the one that appears first in s1. If no such substring exists, return an empty string. Note: Both the strings contain only lowercase english letters.

title: Account Merge
description: Given a 2D array arr[][] of size n , where each element arr[i] is an array of strings representing an account, where the first element arr[i][0] is a name, and the rest of the elements are emails associated with this name. Two accounts belong to the same person if there is a common email associated with both accounts. A person can have any number of accounts initially, but all have the same name. Merge these accounts and return them in the following format: the first element of each account is the name, and the rest of the elements are emails in lexicographically sorted order. Note: Accounts themselves can be returned in any order. Even if two accounts have the same name, they may belong to different people as different people could have the same name.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000 2 ≤ arr[i].size ≤ 10 1 ≤ arr[i][j].size ≤ 30 arr[i][0] consists of English letters.

title: Stickler Thief II
description: You are given an array arr[] which represents houses arranged in a circle, where each house has a certain value. A thief aims to maximize the total stolen value without robbing two adjacent houses. Determine the maximum amount the thief can steal. Note: Since the houses are in a circle, the first and last houses are also considered adjacent .

title: Array to Linked List
description: You are given an array arr[] of integers . You have to construct a singly linked list from the elements of the arr[] and return the head of the linked list.

title: Introduction to Trees
description: Given an integer i . Print the maximum number of nodes on level i of a binary tree. Note : The level of a binary tree starts with 1 (i.e., level 1 contains the root of the tree, level 2 contains the children of the root, and so on).

title: Insert Interval
description: Geek has an array of non-overlapping intervals intervals[][] where intervals[i] = [start i , end i ] represent the start and the end of the i th event and intervals is sorted in ascending order by start i . He wants to add a new interval newInterval[] = [newStart, newEnd] where newStart and newEnd represent the start and end of this interval. Help Geek to insert newInterval into intervals such that intervals is still sorted in ascending order by start i and intervals still does not have any overlapping intervals (merge overlapping intervals if necessary).
constraints: 1 ≤ intervals.size() ≤  10 5 0 ≤ start i ≤ end i ≤ 10 9 0 ≤ newStart ≤ newEnd ≤ 10 9

title: Pass by Reference and Value
description: Geek is learning about functions and calling a function with arguments. He learns that passing can take one of two forms: pass by value or pass by reference. Geek wishes to add 1 and 2, respectively, to the parameter passed by value and reference. Help Geek in fulfilling his goal. Example 1:
constraints: 1 <= a,b <= 10 5 Your Task: You don't need to read input or print anything. Your task is to complete the function passedBy() which takes a and b as input parameters and returns array of two required integers. Expected Time Complexity: O(1) Expected Auxiliary Space: O(1)

title: Shortest Job first
description: The shortest job first (SJF) or shortest job next, is a scheduling policy that selects the waiting process with the smallest execution time to execute next. Given an array of integers bt[] of size n . Array bt[] denotes the burst time of each process. Calculate the average waiting time of all the processes and return the nearest integer which is smaller or equal to the output. Note: Consider all process are available at time 0.

title: Implementation of Priority Queue using Binary Heap
description: Given a binary heap implementation of Priority Queue. Extract the maximum element from the queue i.e. remove it from the Queue and return it's value. Examples :

title: Partition Array for Maximum Sum
description: Given an integer array arr[] and an integer k , partition the array into contiguous subarrays such that each subarray has a length of at most k. After partitioning, replace every element in each subarray with the maximum element present in that subarray. Compute the maximum possible sum of the array after performing this operation. Examples :

title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
description: Given an n × m binary matrix mat[][] , count the total number of square submatrices whose every element is 1 . Examples :

title: Maximum XOR With an Element From Array
description: You are given an array arr[] , containing non-negative integers. Additionally, you have q queries represented as a 2D array queries[][] , where each query is of the form [x i , m i ] . For each query, your task is to find the maximum bitwise XOR value between x i and any element in arr[] that is less than or equal to m i. In other words, for each query [x i , m i ] , compute: max( arr[j] XOR x i ) for all j such that arr[j] ≤ m i . If there is no element in arr[] that satisfies the condition arr[j] ≤ m i , then the answer for that query should be -1 . Return an array ans[] , where ans[i] represents the result of the i-th query .
constraints: 1 ≤ arr.size(), q ≤ 10 5 0 ≤ arr[i] , x i , m i ≤ 10 9

title: Size of a Complete  Binary Tree
description: You are given the root of a complete binary tree. Your task is to find the count of nodes. A complete binary tree is a binary tree whose, all levels except the last one are completely filled, the last level may or may not be completely filled and Nodes in the last level are as left as possible. Note : Design an algorithm that runs better than O(n).
constraints: 0 ≤ N (number of nodes) ≤ 5 * 10 4 0 ≤ value of nodes ≤ 5 * 10 4 The tree is guaranteed to be complete.

title: Count Graphs with n Vertices
description: Given an integer n representing number of vertices. Find out how many undirected graphs (not necessarily connected) can be constructed out of a given n number of vertices.

title: Longest String Chain
description: You are given an array of words where each word consists of lowercase English letters. word A is a predecessor of word B if and only if we can insert exactly one letter anywhere in word A without changing the order of the other characters to make it equal to word B . For example, "abc" is a predecessor of "ab a c" , while "cba" is not a predecessor of "bcad" . A word chain is a sequence of words [word 1 , word 2 , ..., word k ] with k >= 1 , where word 1 is a predecessor of word 2 , word 2 is a predecessor of word 3 , and so on. A single word is trivially a word chain with k = 1 . Return the length of the longest possible word chain with words chosen from the given list of words in any order .
constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 10 4 1 <= words[i].length <= 10 words[i] only consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Print Longest Increasing Subsequence
description: You are given an array of integers arr[] , return the Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) of the given array. LIS is the longest subsequence where each element is strictly greater than the previous one. Note: If multiple LIS of the same maximum length exist, return the one that appears first based on the lexicographical order of their indices (i.e., the earliest combination of positions from the original sequence).

title: Chocolates Pickup
description: You are given a 2D matrix grid[][] of size n*m , where each cell grid[i][j] represents the number of chocolates available at position (i, j) . Two robots are collecting chocolates from this grid: Robot 1 starts at the top-left corner (0, 0) Robot 2 starts at the top-right corner (0, m - 1) Your task is to determine the maximum total number of chocolates both robots can collect while following these rules: From a cell (i, j) , robots can move to cell (i + 1, j - 1) , (i + 1, j) , or (i + 1, j + 1) . When a robot visits a cell, it collects all the chocolates there. If both robots land on the same cell, the chocolates in that cell are collected only once. Robots cannot move outside the boundaries of the grid. Both robots must continue moving until they reach the bottom row of the grid.

title: Minimum Swaps to Group 1s in Circular
description: Given a circular binary array arr[] consisting of only 0s and 1s , find the minimum swaps required to group all the 1s together at any position in the array. In a circular array, the first and the last elements are considered adjacent.

title: Partitions with Given Difference
description: Given an array arr[] and an integer diff , count the number of ways to partition the array into two subsets such that the difference between their sums is equal to diff. Note: A partition in the array means dividing an array into two subsets say S 1 and S 2 such that the union of S 1 and S 2 is equal to the original array and each element is present in only one of the subsets. Examples :

title: Strings with  More Distinct Subsequences
description: Given a pair of strings s1 and s2 of equal lengths, your task is to find which of the two strings has more distinct subsequences. If both strings have the same number of distinct subsequences, return s1 .

title: Triangle Path Sum
description: Given a triangle array, return the minimum path sum to reach from top to bottom . For each step, you may move to an adjacent number of the row below. More formally, if you are on index i on the current row , you may move to either index i or index i + 1 on the next row.

title: Binary Tree Representation
description: Given an array nodes[] of size n , where each element represents the value of a node in the level-order traversal of a complete binary tree, construct the complete binary tree and return its root node.

title: Largest Divisible Subset
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers. Your task is to find the largest subset such that for every pair of elements (x, y) in the subset, either x divides y or y divides x. Note : If multiple subsets of the same maximum length exist, return the one that is lexicographically greatest , after sorting the subset in ascending order.

title: Minimum Subtraction to Make All 0
description: Given a non-negative integer array arr[] . In one operation, you must: Choose a positive integer x such that x is less than or equal to the smallest non-zero element in arr[]. Subtract x from every positive element in arr[]. Return the minimum number of operations required to make every element of the array equal to 0.

title: Bird and Max Fruit Gathering
description: Given an array arr[] representing the fruit values of trees arranged in a circle and an integer m , f ind the maximum total fruits the bird can collect by visiting at most m trees. Bird can start from any tree and move to a neighboring tree. The first and last trees are also considered neighbors. The bird collects the fruit value of every tree it visits.

title: Minimize the sum
description: Given an array arr[] of n integers, repeatedly perform the following operation until only one element remains in the array: Remove any two elements from the array. Compute their sum and add it to the answer. Insert the computed sum back into the array. Return the minimum possible value of the total sum obtained by performing the above operations.

title: Maximum GCD of K Partition Sums
description: Given an array arr[] and an integer k, partition the array into exactly k non-empty contiguous subarrays such that the GCD of their sums is maximized. Return the maximum possible GCD.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 4 , n is length of the array 1 ≤ k ≤ n 1 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10 5

title: Smallest Rearrangement with No "cba" Subsequence
description: Given a string s of lowercase English letters, rearrange the characters of s such that it does not contain "cba" as a subsequence . Among all valid rearrangements, return the lexicographically smallest one.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 s contains only lowercase English alphabets.

title: Absolute Difference Divisible by K
description: Given an integer array arr[] and an integer k . Count the number of pairs (i , j) such that: (i < j). The absolute difference between arr[i] and arr[j] is divisible by k.

title: Make array elements unique
description: Given an integer array arr[ ] , your task is to find the minimum number of increment operations required to make all the array elements unique . i.e. no value in the array should occur more than once. In one operation, a value can be incremented by 1 only. Note: The answer will always fit into a 32-bit integer. Examples :

title: Count Lucky Permutations
description: Given an integer array arr[] of size n and an undirected, unweighted graph with n vertices labeled from 1 to n, described by m edges in graph[][] (where graph[][] is a list of edges). Since each value in arr[] lies between 1 and n, every element of arr[] corresponds to a vertex label in the graph. A permutation p[] of arr[] is called lucky if, for every pair of consecutive elements p[i] and p[i+1] (0 ≤ i < n-1), there exists an edge between vertex p[i] and vertex p[i+1] in the graph. Return the total number of lucky permutations of arr[].
constraints: 2 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 15 1 ≤ m ≤ (n*(n - 1))/2 1 ≤  arr[i], graph[i][j] ≤ n There are no self-loops and repeated edges in the graph.

title: Substrings with more 1's than 0's
description: Given a binary string s consists only of 0s and 1s. Calculate the number of substrings that have more 1s than 0s.

title: Next Greater Element in Circular Array
description: Given a circular integer array arr[] , the task is to determine the next greater element (NGE) for each element in the array. The next greater element of an element arr[i] is the first element that is greater than arr[i] when traversing circularly. If no such element exists, return -1 for that position. Note: Since the array is circular, after reaching the last element, the search continues from the beginning until we have looked at all elements once.

title: Parent of Siblings with Maximum GCD
description: Given a binary tree, find the value of the node whose two immediate children have the maximum GCD. If multiple nodes have the same maximum GCD, return the maximum value among those nodes. A node is considered only if it has both a left and a right child. Return 0 if no such node exists.
constraints: 1 <= Number of nodes <= 10 5 1 <= Data of a node <= 10 5

title: First Node of Loop in Linked List
description: You are given the head of a singly linked list. If a loop is present in the linked list then return the first node of the loop else return -1 . Note: Internally, pos(1 based index) is used to denote the position of the node that tail's next pointer is connected to. If pos = 0, it means the last node points to null, indicating there is no loop. Note that pos is not passed as a parameter.

title: Minimum Carpet Folds to Fit in Box
description: A carpet has dimensions a * b, and a box has dimensions c * d. Find the minimum number of folds moves required to fit the carpet inside the box. In one move, either the length or breadth of the carpet can be replaced by half of its current value using floor division. The carpet can be rotated by 90 degrees any number of times without counting as a move.

title: Maximum Weight Node
description: Given a maze with n cells. Each cell may have multiple entry points but not more than one exit point (i.e entry/exit points are unidirectional doors like valves). You are given an array exits[] , where exits[i] contains the exit point of the ith cell. If exits[i] is -1, then ith cell doesn't have an exit. The task is to find the cell with maximum weight (The weight of a cell i is the sum of all the cell indexes that have exit point as i ). If there are multiple cells with the maximum weight return the cell with highest index. Note: The cells are indexed with an integer value from 0 to n-1. A cell i has weight 0 if no cell has exit point as i.

title: Minimum XOR with given set bits
description: Given two integers a and b , find an integer x such that the number of set bits in x is equal to the number of set bits in b, and the value of (x XOR a) is minimized . Return the value of x .

title: Remove Consecutive Two Same
description: Given a string s , repeatedly remove all adjacent duplicate character pairs until no such pairs remain. Return the resulting string, or "-1" if the string becomes empty . Examples :

title: Minimum Number Of Sprinkler
description: Given a one-dimensional garden of length n. In each position of the n length garden, a sprinkler has been installed. Given an array arr[] such that arr[i] describes the coverage limit of the i th sprinkler. A sprinkler can cover the range from the position max(i - arr[i], 1) to min(i + arr[i], n) . In beginning, all the sprinklers are switched off. The task is to find the minimum number of sprinklers needed to be activated such that the whole n -length garden can be covered by water. Note: Array is 1-based indexed. Example 1:

title: Type it!
description: Geek is extremely punctual but today even he is not feeling like doing his homework assignment. He must start doing it immediately in order to meet the deadline. For the assignment, Geek needs to type a string s . To reduce his workload, he has decided to perform one of the following two operations till he gets the string. Append a character at the end of the string. Append the string formed thus far to the end of the string. (This can not be done more than once.) Help Geek find the minimum operations required to type the given string. Example 1:

title: Minimum Edge Deletions to Make a Star Tree
description: Given a connected undirected tree represented as a parent array arr[], where arr[0] = -1 (node 0 is the root) and arr[i] is the parent of node i, find the minimum moves required to transform the tree into a star tree. A star tree has exactly one center node, and all other nodes are directly connected to the center. In one move, you can merge any two adjacent nodes - the edge between them is deleted and both nodes become a single node.
constraints: 1 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 10 5 0 ≤ arr[i] < arr.size() arr[0] = -1 (node 0 is always the root)

title: Minimum AND Operations to Make Same
description: Given two non-negative integers a and b , f ind the minimum number of the operations to make a and b equal. In one operation, Choose any non-negative integer x . Select either a or b, and replace the selected number with the result of its bitwise AND with x. In other words, you can perform either a = a & x or b = b & x .

title: Find the longest string
description: Given an array of strings words [] . Find the longest string in words[] such that every prefix of it is also present in the array words[]. Note: If multiple strings have the same maximum length, return the lexicographically smallest one .

title: Max Profit Non-Overlapping Intervals
description: Given a list of intervals of size of n, where each interval is represented as [s, e, p] denoting the start time s, end time e, and profit p, find the maximum total profit that can be obtained by selecting a subset of non-overlapping intervals. Two intervals are non-overlapping if the end time of one interval is less than or equal to the start time of the other. Examples :

description: Given N nodes of a tree and a list of edges. Find the minimum number of nodes to be selected to light up all the edges of the tree. An edge lights up when at least one node at the end of the edge is selected. Example 1:
constraints: 1 ≤ N ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ edges ≤ N Given graph is a valid tree.

title: Minimum repeat to make substring
description: Given two strings s1 and s2 . Return a minimum number of times s1 has to be repeated such that s2 is a substring of it. If s2 can never be a substring then return -1 . Note: Both the strings contain only lowercase letters.

title: Paint N Houses
description: There are n houses arranged in a row. Each house must be painted using exactly one of three colors: red, green, or blue. The cost of painting the i-th house with each color is given by three arrays: r[i] — cost of painting house i red g[i] — cost of painting house i green b[i] — cost of painting house i blue Paint all the houses such that no two adjacent houses have the same color. Return the minimum total cost required to paint all n houses while satisfying this condition.

title: Largest Sum Cycle
description: Given a maze with N cells. Each cell may have multiple entry points but not more than one exit(i.e entry/exit points are unidirectional doors like valves). You are given an array Edge[] of N integers, where Edge[i] contains the cell number that can be reached from of cell i in one step. Edge[i] is -1 if the ith cell doesn't have an exit. The task is to find the largest sum of a cycle in the maze(Sum of a cycle is the sum of the cell indexes of all cells present in that cycle). Note: The cells are named with an integer value from 0 to N-1. If there is no cycle in the graph then return -1. Example 1:

title: Intersection Point in Y Shaped Linked Lists
description: You are given the head pointers of two singly linked lists, head1 and head2 . Find and return the exact node where the two linked lists merge into one. If the two lists never merge, return NULL.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 10 5 , where n and m denote the number of nodes in the first and second linked lists respectively. 0 ≤ node->data ≤ 10 5

title: Sum of Vertically Below Descendants
description: Given a Binary Search Tree (BST) with distinct values and an integer target, find the sum of the values of all descendant nodes that lie vertically below the target node. Here vertically below is defined by horizontal distance from root. For example, in the below diagram, 5, 6 and 11 are vertically below 1 because the horizontal distance is 0 for these descendants of 1. Similarly 9 and 8 are vertically below 3. If the target node is not present in the BST, return -1.

title: Longest Subarray Positive Product
description: Given an array arr[] consisting of n integers , find the length of the longest subarray with positive (non zero) product.

title: Count 0s After Setting Rows and Columns as 1
description: You are given an integer n representing an n × n matrix initially filled with 0s. You are also given an integer k and a 2D array arr[][] of size k × 2, where each row contains a pair of 1-based coordinates (r, c) . Perform the k tasks sequentially in the given order. For each task: Set all cells in the rth row to 1. Set all cells in the cth column to 1. Return an array containing the number of 0s remaining after each task.

title: Maximum Bipartite Matching
description: There are m job applicants and n job openings. Each applicant is interested in a subset of the available jobs. You are given a binary matrix mat[][] of size m × n , where: mat[i][j] = 1 indicates that the i-th applicant is interested in the j-th job. mat[i][j] = 0 indicates that the applicant is not interested in that job. Each job can be assigned to only one applicant, and each applicant can be assigned to at most one job. Determine the maximum number of applicants that can be assigned jobs according to their interests.

title: Balloon Everywhere
description: Bob is very fond of balloons. Once he visited an amusement park with his mother. The mother told Bob that she would buy him a balloon only if he answer her problem right. She gave Bob a string s [contains only lowercase characters] and asked him to use the characters of string to form as many instances of the word "balloon" as possible. Return the maximum number of instances that can be formed. Help Bob to solve the problem. Note: You can use each character in the string at most once .

title: Minimum Days
description: Given a string s of length n containing only lowercase English letters, and a permutation p[] of length n containing integers from 0 to n - 1. On the (i + 1)th day, the character at index p[i] in the string is replaced with '?'. For example: On day 1, replace s[p[0]] with '?'. On day 2, replace s[p[1]] with '?'. On day 3, replace s[p[2]] with '?'. And so on. Find the minimum number of days after which the string satisfies the following condition for every index i (0 ≤ i < n - 1): If s[i] != '?', then s[i] != s[i + 1]. Examples :
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 0 ≤ p[i] ≤ n-1 s.length == n s contains only lowercase alphabets.

title: Prime List
description: Given a linked list, replace all the values with the nearest prime number. If more than one prime number exists at an equal distance, choose the smallest one. Return the head of the modified linked list. Examples :

title: Walls Coloring
description: There are n walls in Geeksland. Each wall can be painted with one of three colors: pink , black, or yellow. The cost of painting the i th wall with each color is given by colors[i][0], colors[i][1], and colors[i][2], respectively. Find the minimum total cost to paint all the walls such that no two adjacent walls have the same color.

title: Greater on Left and Smaller on Right
description: Given an array arr[] of size n , for each index i, find the absolute difference between the following two values: Count of Strictly Greater on Left Count of Strictly Smaller on Right
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 -10 9 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10 9 Array can contain duplicate elements.

title: Towers Reaching Both Stations
description: Given a matrix mat[][] of size n x m , where mat[i][j] represents the signal strength of a communication tower. Two control stations monitor the network: Station P covers the top and left boundaries of the grid. Station Q covers the bottom and right boundaries of the grid. A signal can propagate from a tower to one of its neighbouring towers in the four directions (North, South, East, and West) only if the neighbouring tower has a signal strength less than or equal to that of the current tower. Determine the number of towers (x, y) from which a signal can eventually reach both Station P and Station Q. Any tower located on a boundary covered by a station can transmit directly to that station.

title: Shortest Path Using Atmost One Curved Edge
description: Given an undirected, connected graph with V vertices numbered from 0 to V-1 and E double-edges, represented as a 2D array edges[][] . Each double-edge is represented by a tuple (x, y, w1, w2) , which indicates that there are two edges between vertices x and y : a straight edge with weight w1 and a curved edge with weight w2 . You are given two vertices a and b and you have to go from a to b through a series of edges such that in the entire path, you can use at most 1 curved edge . Your task is to find the shortest path from a to b satisfying the above condition. If no such path exists that satisfies this restriction, return -1 . Note: It is guaranteed that the shortest path value will fit in a 32-bit integer.

title: Unique Paths in a Grid
description: Given a grid grid[][] of size n × m containing values 0 and 1 having the following meanings: 0 represents an open cell through which movement is allowed. 1 represents a blocked cell that cannot be traversed. Starting from the top-left cell (0, 0), find the total number of distinct paths to reach the bottom-right cell (n - 1, m - 1). From any cell, movement is allowed only in the right and down directions, and a path is valid only if it passes through open cells. Note: It is guaranteed that the answer fits within a 32-bit integer.

title: Valid Compressed String
description: Given two strings s and t , where s is the original string and t is its compressed form, find if t is a valid compression of s or not. During compression, any sequence of consecutive characters may be replaced by the number of characters removed. If t contains consecutive digits, treat them as a single number. For example, "B32" represents "B" + "32", not "B" + "3" + "2".
constraints: 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 10 6 1 ≤ |t| ≤ 10 6 All characters are either capital or numeric.

title: Minimum Iterations to Fill a Grid from One Cell
description: Given an n × m matrix that contains all 0s except for a single cell at position (x, y) , which contains 1 , find the minimum number of iterations required to fill the entire matrix with 1s. In one iteration, every cell containing 1 simultaneously converts its four adjacent cells (up, down, left, and right) to 1 Note : The position (x, y) uses 1-based indexing.

title: Reverse Two Parts of Linked List
description: Given the head of a linked list and an integer k , reverse the first k nodes and separately reverse the remaining n - k nodes of the linked list.
constraints: 1 ≤ size of linked list ≤ 10 6 1 ≤ node->data ≤ 10 6 1 ≤  k < size of linked list

title: Number of Good Components
description: Given an undirected graph with v vertices(numbered from 1 to v ) and e edges. Find the number of good components in the graph. A component of the graph is good if and only if the component is fully connected. Note: A fully connected component is a subgraph of a given graph such that there's an edge between every pair of vertices in the component. The given graph can be disconnected .

title: Avoid Explosion
description: Given two 2D integer arrays mix[][] and danger[][] : mix[i] = [x, y] means solutions x and y are to be mixed in that order. danger[i] = [p, q] means if solutions p and q ever become part of the same mixture, an explosion will occur. Process the pairs in mix from left to right. For each pair, return: " true " if mixing that pair is safe. " false " if mixing that pair would cause an explosion. Once a pair is found unsafe, it is not mixed, but all previously mixed solutions remain and may affect later pairs. Return an array answer, where answer[i] is "true" if mix[i] can be safely processed and "false" otherwise.
constraints: 1 ≤ mix.length ≤ 1000, 1 ≤ danger.length ≤ 1000 1 ≤ mix[i][0], mix[i][1] ≤ 1000 1 ≤ danger[i][0], danger[i][1] ≤ 1000 mix[i].length = 2 danger[i].length = 2 mix[i][0] != mix[i][1] danger[i][0] != danger[i][1]

title: Equalize All Prefix Sums
description: Given a sorted array arr[] . For each i(0 ≤ i ≤ n-1), make all the elements of the array from index 0 to i equal , using the minimum number of operations . In one operation you either increase or decrease the array element by 1 . Return an array that contains the minimum number of operations for each i, to accomplish the above task. Note: For each index i, consider the original array without applying modifications made for previous indices. Try to solve the problem using O(1) extra space (excluding the resultant array). Examples :
constraints: 1 ≤ arr.size() ≤ 10 5 -10 4 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10 4 Sum of n over all test case does not exceed 10 6 .

title: Max Alternating Sum Path to a Leaf
description: You are given a rooted tree consisting of n nodes, numbered from 1 to n . The tree is represented by an array par[] of size n , where par[i] denotes the parent of node i+1, and par[0] = -1 since node 1 is the root. You are also given an array val[] of size n , where val[i] represents the value of node i+1. You may choose any node in the tree as the starting node. From the current node, you can move only to one of its children. Continue moving in this manner until you reach a leaf node. The sequence of node values encountered along the chosen path forms an array b . For a path with value sequence b = [b1, b2, ..., bk], define its alternating sum as: f(b) = b1 - b2 + b3 - b4 + ... + (-1)^(k-1) × bk Determine the maximum possible value of f(b) among all valid paths.

title: Update Queries
description: Given an integer n , consider an array of n elements, initially all set to 0. You are also given a 2D array queries[][] of size q × 3, where each queries[i] contains three integers [l, r, x]. For each query [l, r, x], perform the following operation: For every index i such that l ≤ i ≤ r, update a[i] as: a[i] = a[i] | x where | denotes the bitwise OR operation. After performing all q queries in the given order, return the final array arr[]. Note: The indices l and r are 1-based and both endpoints are included in the range.

title: Walls Coloring with K Colors
description: Given n walls arranged in a row, and each wall must be painted using one of the k available colors. The cost of painting i-th wall with j-th color is given by costs[i][j] . Find the minimum total cost required to paint all the walls in such a way that no two adjacent walls share the same color. If it is impossible to paint the walls under this condition, return -1 .

title: Cutting Rectangles
description: Given the dimensions l and b of a rectangle, cut it into identical squares of the largest possible side length such that no part of the rectangle remains uncovered. Return a list containing two integers: the minimum number of squares required and the side length of each square. Examples :

title: Good Stones
description: Given an array arr[] , where arr[i] represents the exact number of steps to move from index i, determine the number of good indices. A positive value indicates a move to the right, while a negative value indicates a move to the left. An index is considered good if repeatedly following the jumps eventually takes you outside the array. Otherwise, if the jumps result in an infinite loop, the index is considered bad. Return the number of good indices.

title: Remove Redundant Parenthesis
description: Given a valid expression containing only binary operators '+', '-', '*', '/' and operands, remove all the redundant parenthesis. A set of parenthesis is said to be redundant if, removing them, does not change the value of the expression. Note: The operators '+' and '-' have the same priority. '*' and '/' also have the same priority. '*' and '/' have more priority than '+' and '-' . Example 1:
constraints: 1 < Length of Exp < 10 5 Exp contains uppercase English letters, '(' , ')', '+', '-', '*' and '/'.

title: Frogs and Jumps
description: Frogs are positioned at one end of a pond, and each wants to reach the other end. The pond has some leaves arranged in a straight line. Each frog has a strength s , meaning it jumps exactly s leaves at a time - for example, a frog with strength 2 visits leaves 2, 4, 6, and so on while crossing the pond. Given the strength of each frog (as an array arr[] ) and the total number of leaves k , find how many leaves are not visited by any frog after all frogs have crossed the pond.

title: Maximum Intersecting Lines
description: You are given a 2D array lines[][] , where each row [l, r] represents a horizontal line segment on the X-axis with endpoints at x = l and x = r (both inclusive). Return the maximum number of horizontal line segments that can be intersected by a single vertical line.

title: Max Profit by Removing pr or rp
description: Given a string s . In one operation, you can remove the substring "pr" from the string s and get amount x or you can remove the substring "rp" and get the amount y . Find the maximum amount you can get if you perform zero or more such operations optimally.

title: Partition Into 4 with Min Sum Diff
description: Given an array arr[] , partition it into four non-empty contiguous subarrays P , Q , R , and S . Let the sums of these subarrays be W , X , Y , and Z , respectively. Find the minimum possible value of max(W, X, Y, Z) - min(W, X, Y, Z) over all valid partitions.

title: Knight in Geekland
description: A knight is stationed at position (x, y) in Geekland, represented as an n×m matrix, where each cell holds some points. At the i-th step, the knight can collect the total points from all cells reachable in exactly i knight-moves (moving the same way a knight moves on a chessboard), without revisiting any cell. The knight also has a magical power to pull points from the future: if he collects y points at step x, he can absorb all the points collectable at step (x + y) as well, without spending an additional step. If step (x + y) itself yields z points, he can further absorb step (x + y + z), and so on, while always remaining at step x and collecting the cumulative total of every step reachable this way. Find the minimum step count that yields the maximum total points collectable this way. Note: The knight moves exactly like a knight on a chessboard . Indexing is 0-based.

title: Count Chocolates Bought with k Coins
description: Geek has k coins and wants to buy chocolates from a shop. The shop has different types of chocolates whose prices are given in a sorted array price[] in increasing order. There is an infinite supply of every type of chocolate. Geek always buys the costliest chocolate he can afford. After buying a chocolate, its price is deducted from the remaining coins. He repeats this process until he cannot afford any chocolate. Return the total number of chocolates Geek buys. Note: All chocolate prices are pairwise distinct.

title: Divide in Incremental Groups
description: Given two integers n and k , count the number of ways to divide n into groups of positive integers, such that each group shall have k elements and their sum is n . Also the number of elements in the groups follows a non-decreasing order (i.e. group[i] <= group[i+1]). Find the number of such groups

description: You are given an integer N . Consider an array arr having N elements where arr[i] = 2*i+1 . (The array is 0-indexed) You are allowed to perform the given operation on the array any number of times: 1) Select two indices i and j and increase arr[i] by 1 and decrease arr[j] by 1. Your task is to find the minimum number of such operations required to make all the elements of the array equal. Example 1:

description: Given an array of positive integers arr[] . You need to find the count of the special numbers in arr[]. A number is said to be a special number if it is divisible by atleast one other element of arr[]. Examples :

title: Minimum Steps Required
description: Given a string str consisting of only two characters 'a' and 'b' . You need to find the minimum steps required to make the string empty by removing consecutive a's and b's .

title: Make Array Beautiful
description: Given an array of negative and non-negative integers. You need to make the array beautiful. An array is beautiful if two adjacent integers, arr[i] and arr[i+1] are either negative or positive. You can do the following operation any number of times until the array becomes beautiful. If two adjacent are different i.e. one of them is negative and other is positive, remove them. Return the beautiful array after performing the above operation. An empty array is also a beautiful array. There can be multiple beautiful output arrays. For consistencty with the test cases, scan the array from left to right for removing two adjacent. Note: 0 is considered a positive number in this context.

title: Remainder on Division by 11
description: Given a big positive number x represented as string, find value of x mod 11.

title: Nth Geeky Number
description: Geek has defined a sequence called Geeky Numbers. The first k terms of the sequence are given in the array geekNum[]. Every subsequent term is equal to the sum of the previous k terms. Given integers n and k , and the array geekNum[] , return the nth term of the Geeky sequence. Note: The sequence uses 1-based indexing.

title: Minimum Platforms 2
description: Given three arrays arr[] , dep[] , and days[] , where: arr[i] is the arrival time of the i-th train, dep[i] is the departure time of the i-th train, and days[i] is the day on which the i-th train runs, and an integer k representing the number of available railway platforms, determine whether all trains can be accommodated without any train having to wait. Each train arrives and departs on the same day. Return true if all trains can be scheduled using at most k platforms; otherwise, return false . Note: If a train departs at the exact time another train arrives on the same day, the departing train vacates the platform first, so the arriving train can use the same platform. Time values are ordinary integers and should be compared numerically. They do not follow the standard HHMM format. For example, 2398 > 2368, and 2368 does not represent 23:68. Examples :
