Each person can make at most jumps[i] jumps, and no one can move beyond the last tower. You are also given a query array queries[] . For each query queries[i], find how many people can reach a tower with height greater than or equal to queries[i].

title: Min Area of Rectangle
description: Geek is given a string path consisting of the characters 'U', 'D', 'L' and 'R' . These characters represent movements in a 2D grid, where the top left corner is (0, 0). 'D' : Move one cell down. 'U' : Move one cell up. 'R' : Move one cell right. 'L' : Move one cell left. Initially, Geek is at cell (0, 0) in a rectangle grid of size n * m (where n represents the number of rows and m represents the number of columns). Note that n and m are not provided as inputs and must be determined by you to satisfy the conditions described : - Geek must follow the movements in the path string in order. However, if a movement causes Geek to step outside the boundaries of the rectangle grid, he remains in his current cell instead of moving. Given the final cell (fr, fc) that geek must reach by following the entire path, determine the minimum possible area of the rectangle, n * m that allows geek to complete the path and reach (fr, fc) at the end. If it is not possible for Geek to reach the target cell (fr, fc) using the given path, return -1 .
constraints: 1 ≤ | path | ≤ 2*10 5 0 ≤ fr, fc < 10 5 path consists only of 'D', 'U', 'R' and 'L'

title: Make All Zero
description: Two players are playing a game involving energy stacks. Each stack contains a certain number of energy crystals represented as integers in an array arr[] . Players take turns. On each turn, a player must remove one entire stack (i.e., remove one element from the array). However, there's a special rule: If the bitwise XOR of the entire array is 0 before a player's turn, then that player instantly wins. If it's not zero, they must remove one stack. The game continues until someone wins either due to the XOR rule or because the other player cannot move. Both players play optimally. You need to determine who will win for each initial array of stacks. Return true if Player second wins otherwise return false .

title: Count Valid Pairs
description: You are given a graph with n nodes, where each node i has a weight w[i] . U ndirected edges are present between two nodes i and j (i ≠ j) if and only if: w[i] & w[j] ≠ 0, where "&" represents the Bitwise AND operation. The task is to find the total number of valid pairs in the graph. A pair of nodes (i, j), where (i < j), is called a valid pair if there exists a path between the nodes i and j.

title: Longest Bit-Increasing Subsequence
description: Given an array arr[] of positive integers. Find out the longest bit-increasing subsequence of arr[]. A subsequence b[] of an array is called bit-increasing if setBitCount(b[0]) ^ setBitCount(b[1]) ^ ... ^ setBitCount(b[i-1]) <= setBitCount(b[i]) for all 1 <= i < |b|, where setBitCount(x) is the number of ones in the binary representation of x. Return an array which is the longest bit-increasing subsequence of arr[]. Note: You can return any longest bit-increasing subsequence. If your answer is correct, you will see the length of the longest bit-increasing subsequence as the output, else -1. Examples :

title: Card Flip
description: Given n cards arranged in a row. Each card has a number on the front and back, represented by two integer arrays front[] and back[] . For the i-th card, front[i] is the number on the front and back[i] is the number on the back. Initially, all cards are placed with their front side visible. You can perform the following operation on the cards. Choose any card at position i (1 ≤ i < n) and swap it with the card at position ( i +1). After swapping, flip both cards so that the opposite side becomes visible. Determine the minimum number of operations required to arrange the cards such that the numbers on the visible sides are in non-decreasing order. If arranging the cards in non-decreasing order is impossible, return -1.

title: Unique Node Counts
description: Geek finds out a unique tree in a dense forest. The tree consists of n nodes, numbered from 1 to n , and each node has an initial length of 0. Geek observes the tree for d days and records how the length of the nodes changes. You are given arr[][], where arr[i][0] represent the node number and arr[i][1] represents the length increased in that node for the ith day. For each day from 1 to d , determine how many unique node lengths are present in the tree. Examples :

title: Odd Equals Even Path
description: Given a tree of n nodes, rooted at node 0 . Each node is numbered from 0 to n-1. Also given a 2D integer array edges[][] of size n-1 where each edges[i] = [u i , v i ] denotes that there is an edge between nodes u i and v i in the tree. Find the number of paths starting from each subtree rooted at node i (0 ≤ i < n) such that the count of odd nodes in the path is equal to the count of even nodes in the path. Return an array of size n, where the i-th element is the number of such paths starting from the subtree rooted at node i. Note: The maximum depth of the tree is atmost 200.

title: Longest Colored Path
description: Given an undirected acyclic graph (tree) with n nodes numbered from 1 to n. Each node is colored either Red (R) or Blue (B). The colors of the nodes are given by a string s of length n, where: s[i] = 'R' means node i + 1 is Red. s[i] = 'B' means node i + 1 is Blue. You are also given a list of n - 1 edges edges[][] , where each edges[i] = [u, v] represents an undirected edge between nodes u and v. You can start from any node and traverse along the edges to form a path. A path is called valid if, once you visit a Blue node, you cannot visit any Red node after it on the same path. In other words, a valid path must have the following form: Only Red nodes, or Only Blue nodes, or Some Red nodes followed by some Blue nodes. A path containing a pattern like Blue -> Red is invalid. Find the maximum number of nodes in a valid path.

title: Equal Islands
description: Given n islands, where the importance value of island i is given by arr[i-1]. Initially, all islands are separate. You are also given a 2D array queries[][] of size q, where each query contains two distinct island numbers u and v. For each query, merge the islands containing u and v. The importance value of the merged island is the sum of their importance values. After all queries, the number of remaining distinct islands is guaranteed to be at most 150. Determine whether these remaining islands can be divided into two non-empty groups such that both groups have the same total importance value. Note: If u and v already belong to the same island, the query has no effect.

title: Santa's Christmas Journey
description: Santa is preparing for Christmas and plans to give presents to n children, each in a separate house. The houses are connected by n - 1 snowy trails, represented by the array trails[] , where each element [u, v] indicates a direct trail between house u and house v . Santa's journey plan is given by an array journeyPlan[] , consists of m routes. Each route is represented by two integers, start_house and end_house , meaning Santa will travel between these houses, passing through all houses along the way and distribute the presents. Your task is to determine how many presents each child will receive after all the journeys in the plan. Note: The village is connected , forming an acyclic graph with exactly n - 1 trails.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 10 5 trails.size() = n - 1 1 ≤ trails[i][j], journey_plan [i][j] ≤ n

title: GeekLand Tour
description: Geek is planning a tour of Geekland, a country with cities numbered from 1 to n . The cities are connected by roads, forming a tree with n cities and n-1 roads . Each city i (1 to n) is located at a location loc[i-1] , where the distance between two cities is the absolute difference of their locations. The roads in Geekland are represented by a list of n-1 bi-directional edges roads , where roads[j] = [u j , v j ] indicates a road between city u and city v . Geek wants to explore Geekland but has no money for traveling. However, a tour agency offers free rides for cities that are within a distance of less than or equal to k . Geek can start his journey from any city and wishes to visit as many cities as possible under given conditions. Your task is to determine the maximum number of cities Geek can visit, without travelling any road more than once.

title: Operations to make palindromic subarray
description: You are given an integer array arr[] . Your task is to consider every subarray of arr[] individually and find the minimum number of operations required to convert each subarray into a palindromic sequence. In one operation, you can change any one element of the subarray to any integer. Operations are local to the subarray and do not affect the original array or any other subarrays. Each subarray is treated independently. A palindromic sequence is one that reads the same forwards and backwards (e.g., [1, 2, 2, 1], [7]). Note: Each number in the array appears at most 100 times .

title: Make Strings Equal
description: Given two strings s and t , consisting of lowercase English letters. You are also given, a 2D array transform[][] , where each entry [x, y] means that you are allowed to transform character x into character y and an array cost[] , where cost[i] is the cost of transforming transform[i][0] into transform[i][1] . You can apply any transformation any number of times on either string. Your task is to find the minimum total cost required to make the strings identical . If it is impossible to make the two strings identical using the available transformations, return -1 .
constraints: 1 ≤ s.size() = t.size() ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ transform.size() = cost.size() ≤ 500 'a' ≤ transform[i][0], transform[i][1] ≤ 'z' 1 ≤ cost[i] ≤ 500

title: Maximum Length Chain of Pairs
description: You are given an array arr[] of n pairs where each pair consists of two integers (a, b) such that a < b . A pair (c, d) can follow another pair (a, b) if and only if b < c . A chain of pairs is a sequence of pairs where each pair can follow the previous one. Return the length of the longest chain that can be formed using the given pairs. You may arrange the pairs in any order.

title: Second Best Minimum Spanning Tree
description: Given an undirected graph of V vertices numbered from (0 to V-1) and E edges represented by a 2D array edges[][] , where each edges[i] contains three integers [u, v, w] , representing an undirected edge from u to v , having weight w . Find the weight of the second best minimum spanning tree of the given graph. If no such second best MST exists, return -1. . A second best MST is defined as the minimum-weight spanning tree whose total weight is strictly greater than the weight of the minimum spanning tree. Note: The graph is connected and does not contain any self-loops or parallel (multiple) edges.

title: Largest Subset of 1 to n with XOR n
description: Given an positive integer n , find a subset of numbers from 1 to n (inclusive), where each number can be used at most once, such that: The XOR of all elements in the subset is exactly n. The size of the subset is as large as possible. If multiple such subsets exist, choose the lexicographically smallest one. A subset a[] is lexicographically smaller than subset b[] if at the first index where they differ, a[i] < b[i] (based on character ASCII). If all elements match but one subset ends earlier, the shorter subset is considered smaller.

title: XOR Pairs less than K
description: Given an array arr[] and an integer k, we need to count the number of pairs from the given array such that the Bitwise XOR of each pair is less than k.

title: Maximise String Score
description: You are given a string s , and a list of jumps[][] of size n, where each jumps[i] = [s1, s2] denotes that you are allowed to jump from character s1 to s2 in the forward direction. Additionally, you are allowed to jump forward from a character to any other occurrence of the same character within the string. You start at index 0 of the string. After every valid jump from index i to index j, where s[i] = s1 and s[j] = s2, you earn a score equal to the sum of ASCII values of all characters between the jump except for the characters equals s2 , i.e. score(i, j) = sum(ascii(s[k]) for i ≤ k < j and s[k] != s[j]). Determine the maximum score that can be achieved by performing a sequence of valid jumps starting from index 0.
constraints: 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 2 * 10 5 1 ≤ jumps.size() ≤ 676 There are atleast two distinct characters in s.

title: Minimum Base Representation
description: Ozha and Teek are close friends, but they often get into arguments about numbers and number systems. Teek strongly dislikes the decimal number system and believes that numbers look far more interesting when written in other bases. To impress Teek and finally settle their debate, Ozha decides to build a Probot that explores number representations in different bases. Teek gives Ozha a natural number M , written in the usual decimal system. Ozha’s task is to convert this number into various numbering systems and find a base B such that when the number M is written in base B , all the digits in its representation are exactly the same. Among all such possible bases, Ozha wants to find the smallest base that satisfies this condition. To convert a number from decimal to base B , Ozha repeatedly divides the number by B and keeps track of the remainders. The digits of the base-B representation are formed from the final quotient followed by these remainders. In some special cases, this representation becomes particularly pleasing to Teek because every digit turns out to be identical, such as when the decimal number 63 is written as 333 in base 4. Ozha hopes that by finding the minimum base B for which the representation of M consists of identical digits, she can finally impress Teek and win their ongoing debate. Your task is to help Ozha determine the minimum base B such that the representation of the given number M in base B contains only one digit repeated .

title: Smallest Missing Number
description: Given a sorted array arr[] , of n distinct integers where each integer is in the range from 0 to m-1 and m > n. Find the smallest number that is missing from the array.

title: Minimum Operation To Make Equal
description: You are given an array arr[] consisting of n elements. At each operation you can select any one element and increase rest of n-1 elements by 1. Your task is to make all elements equal performing such operation as many times as needed. Find the minimum number of operations needed for this.

title: Right-Angled Number Triangle Pattern
description: Given a number n . The task is to print Right-Angled Number Triangle with n lines. Note: There is a space between two adjacent number in the pattern.

title: Solid Rectangle
description: Given two integers n and m , print a solid rectangle pattern of n rows and m columns using the " * " character. Note: There is a space between two adjacent stars (*) in the pattern.

title: Pyramid Pattern
description: Given a number n , print pyramid pattern with n lines.

title: Hollow Diamond
description: Given a number n . Print Hollow Diamond Pattern with n lines. Note: There is a space between two adjacent stars (*) in the pattern.

title: Print Hollow Rectangle
description: Given two integers n and m , print a hollow rectangle pattern consisting of n rows and m columns.

title: Butterfly Pattern
description: Given a number n . Print Butterfly Pattern with n lines.

title: Conway's Game Of Life
description: Consider a binary matrix mat[][] of size m × n , where each cell represents either a dead (0) or live (1) state. This configuration represents a generation, and your task is to compute the next generation of the matrix based on the following rules: Any live cell with fewer than two live (< 2) neighbours dies as if caused by underpopulation. Any live cell with two or three live (= 2 or 3) neighbours lives on to the next generation. Any live cell with more than three live (> 3) neighbours dies, as if by overpopulation. Any dead cell with exactly three live (= 3) neighbours becomes a live cell, as if by reproduction. Neighbours are the cells connected horizontally, vertically, or diagonally to a given cell (i.e., all 8 adjacent cells are considered neighbours). Note: The neighbour cells that lie outside the matrix mat[][] are considered dead. The updation of all cells should be done based on the original values of the matrix, not on the values that are being updated during the process. You do not need to return anything, modify the matrix in-place.

title: Matrix Row-Column Swaps
description: You are given two integers m and n , representing the number of rows and columns of a grid. Initially, the grid is filled with integers from 1 to m × n , arranged sequentially from left to right, top to bottom. In other words, the first row contains the first n numbers, the second row contains the next n, and so on. You are also given a 2D vector queries[][] of size q , where each element is a list of three integers [type, a, b], representing an operation: type = 1 → Exchange the entire a-th row with the b-th row. type = 2 → Exchange the entire a-th column with the b-th column. type = 3 → Report the value currently present at position (a, b) in the grid. Your task is to process all the operations in the given order and return the results for every query of type 3.

title: Longest Balanced Substring
description: Given a string s consisting only of digits, find the length of the longest substring of length 2k (where k ≥ 1) such that the sum of left k digits is equal to the sum of right k digits. If no such valid substring exists, return 0 .
constraints: 1 ≤ s.size() ≤ 2000 s consists only of digits from '0' to '9'.

title: Replace with Adjacent Multiplication
description: Given an array arr[] , replace every element with the product of itself and its adjacent elements. For index i: arr[i] = arr[i-1] * arr[i] * arr[i+1] Assume the previous element of the first element and the next element of the last element as 1. Examples :

title: Ancestor Queries on a Tree
description: Given a tree with n nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1 , rooted at node 0 and an array arr[] , where arr[i] represents the parent of node i. For the root node, arr[0] = -1. Also given a 2D array queries[][] of size q × 2, where each query is of the form [u, k]. For each query, find the k-th ancestor of node u, i.e., the node obtained after moving k times from u to its parent. If the k-th ancestor does not exist, return -1. Return an array containing the answer for each query in the same order.
constraints: 1 ≤ n, q ≤ 10 5 1 ≤ queries[i][0] ≤ n-1 1 ≤ queries[0][1] ≤ n

title: Students Eligible for Graduation
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame students containing information about students, return the student_name, graduation_year, total_credits, and completed_courses of all students who are eligible for graduation. A student is considered eligible for graduation if: The student has earned at least 120 credits. The student has completed at least 30 courses. Return the resulting DataFrame in any order. Pandas Schema : student_id: Unique ID for each student (Primary key). student_name: The name of the student. graduation_year: The year the student is expected to graduate. total_credits: The total number of credits earned by the student. completed_courses: The number of courses the student has completed.

title: High-Rated and Expensive Products
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame products containing information about products, return the product_id, product_name, rating, quantity_in_stock, and price of all products that are high-rated, in stock, and expensive. A product is considered high-rated and expensive if: The product has a rating of at least 4.5. The product is available in stock (quantity_in_stock > 0). The product price is at least 300. Return the resulting DataFrame in any order. Pandas Schema: product_id: Unique ID for each product (Primary key). product_name: The name of the product. rating: The rating of the product (float, ranging from 1 to 5). quantity_in_stock: The number of units available in stock. price: The price of the product. Example : Input table: Output table:

title: Second Highest Salary
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame employee containing employee salary information, find the second highest distinct salary. Return the result as a DataFrame with a single column named SecondHighestSalary. If there is no second highest distinct salary, return None in that column. Pandas Schema: id: Unique ID for each employee (Primary key). salary: The salary of the employee.

title: Rank Scores
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame scores containing player score information, return each score along with its corresponding rank. The ranking should be calculated based on the following rules : Scores are ranked in descending order (highest score gets rank 1). Equal scores receive the same rank. Dense ranking is used, meaning ranks are consecutive integers with no gaps after ties. Return the resulting DataFrame containing the columns score and rank. Pandas Schema: id: Unique ID for each score (Primary key). score: The score of the game (floating point value with two decimal places).

title: Count City Population Categories
description: Given a DataFrame cities containing information about cities and their populations, determine the number of cities that belong to each population category. The population categories are defined as follows: Small City: Population strictly less than 100000. Medium City: Population in the inclusive range [100000, 1000000]. Large City: Population strictly greater than 1000000. Return a DataFrame with the following columns: category: The population category. cities_count: The number of cities belonging to that category. The result must always contain all three categories. If no city belongs to a category, return 0 for that category. Pandas Schema: city_id: Unique ID for each city (Primary key). population: Population of the city.

title: Daily Products and Customers
description: Given a DataFrame activities containing information about product purchases, determine the number of distinct products purchased and distinct customers for each combination of date_id and store_name. For every (date_id, store_name) pair, calculate: unique_products : The number of distinct product_id values. unique_customers: The number of distinct customer_id values. Return a DataFrame containing the columns date_id, store_name, unique_products, and unique_customers in any order. Pandas Schema: date_id: The date when the product was purchased. store_name: The name of the store where the product was purchased. product_id: The unique ID of the product purchased. customer_id: The unique ID of the customer who purchased the product.

title: Number of Unique Projects Worked on by Each Employee
description: Given a DataFrame employee_projects containing information about employees and the projects they work on, determine the number of unique projects worked on by each employee. An employee may be associated with the same project multiple times. Count only the distinct project_id values for each employee. Return a DataFrame containing the columns employee_id and cnt, where cnt is the number of distinct projects associated with the employee. The result can be returned in any order. Pandas Schema: employee_id: The unique ID for each employee. project_id: The unique ID for each project. dept_id: The department ID where the project belongs. The project_id uniquely identifies each project, while dept_id represents the department to which the project belongs.

title: Calculate Discount for Products
description: Given a DataFrame products containing information about products, determine the discount for each product. A product receives a discount equal to its price if product_id is even and category starts with 'A'; otherwise, the discount is 0. Return a DataFrame containing the product_id and corresponding discount for each product, ordered by product_id in ascending order. Pandas Schema: product_id: The unique ID for each product (Primary key). category: The category of the product. price: The price of the product.

title: Patients with Hypertension
description: Given a DataFrame patients containing the columns patient_id, patient_name, and patient_condition, find the patient_id, patient_name, and patient_condition of all patients having Hypertension. A patient is considered to have Hypertension if their patient_condition starts with the prefix HTN. Return the result DataFrame in any order. Pandas Schema: patient_id: Unique ID for each patient (Primary key). patient_name: Name of the patient. patient_condition: The medical condition of the patient. A patient has Hypertension if the condition starts with the prefix HTN.

title: Team Leaders with At Least 4 Members
description: Given a DataFrame employee containing information about employees and their team leaders, find the names of all team leaders who have at least 4 direct reports. An employee is considered a direct report of a team leader if the employee's leaderId is equal to that team leader's id. Return a DataFrame containing the names of all such team leaders. Pandas Schema: id: Unique ID for each employee (Primary key). name: Name of the employee. department: The department where the employee works. leaderId: ID of the employee's team leader (null if the employee has no leader).

title: Eco-Friendly and Low-Calorie Products
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame products containing information about products, find the product_id, product_name, and calories of all products that are eco-friendly and have low calories. A product is considered eco-friendly if its eco_friendly value is 'Y'. A product is considered to have low calories if its calories are less than or equal to 200. Return the resulting DataFrame in any order. Pandas Schema product_id: Unique ID for each product (Primary key). product_name: Name of the product. eco_friendly: Indicates whether the product is eco-friendly ('Y' for Yes, 'N' for No). calories: Number of calories in the product.

title: Frequent Commenters on Own Articles
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame comments containing information about comments made on articles, find all authors who have commented on their own articles more than once. An author is considered to have commented on their own article if author_id is equal to viewer_id. Return a DataFrame containing a single column id, where id is the author_id of each such author. The result should be sorted in ascending order of id. Pandas Schema article_id: Unique ID of the article. author_id: Unique ID of the author of the article. viewer_id: Unique ID of the user who commented on the article. comment_date: Date on which the comment was made.

title: Count Product Categories
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame products containing information about products and their categories, determine the number of products in each category. Return a DataFrame containing the columns category_name and products_count, where products_count is the number of products belonging to each category. The result should be sorted by category_name in ascending order. Pandas Schema product_id: Unique ID of the product (Primary key). category_name: Name of the category to which the product belongs.

title: Salary Trends Across Department
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame employees containing information about employees, determine the mean salary for each department. Return a DataFrame containing the columns department and mean_salary, where mean_salary is the average salary of employees in that department. The result should be sorted by department in ascending order. Pandas Schema employee_id: Unique ID of the employee. department: Department in which the employee works. salary: Salary of the employee.

title: Gender-Based Age Distribution
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame people containing information about people's age and gender, determine the median age for each gender. Return a DataFrame containing the columns gender and median_age, where median_age is the median age of all people belonging to that gender. The result should be sorted by gender in ascending order. Pandas Schema person_id: Unique ID of each person. gender: Gender of the person. age: Age of the person. Example Input table: Output table: Explanation: The resulting DataFrame contains the columns gender and median_age. F (Female): The ages are 22, 27, 30. The median age is 27, which is the middle value after sorting. M (Male): The ages are 23, 25, 28. The median age is 25, which is the middle value after sorting. Hence, the resulting DataFrame contains the median age for each gender, sorted by gender in ascending order.

title: Most Frequent Student Scores
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame scores containing the scores obtained by students, find the score(s) that appear most frequently in the DataFrame. The DataFrame contains the columns student_id and score, where each row represents a student's score. If multiple scores have the same highest frequency, return all such scores. Return a DataFrame containing the columns score and mode, where mode represents the frequency of the corresponding score. The result should be sorted by score in ascending order. Pandas Schema student_id: Unique ID of the student. score: Score obtained by the student.

title: Delete Duplicate Phone Numbers
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame customers containing customer information, remove all duplicate phone numbers while keeping only the customer with the smallest id for each phone number. Return the resulting DataFrame containing the columns id, name, and phone, where each phone number appears only once. The result can be returned in any order. Pandas Schema id: Unique ID of the customer (Primary key). name: Name of the customer. phone: Phone number of the customer.

title: Replace Employee ID with Department ID
description: Given two Pandas DataFrames Employees and EmployeeDept , display the department ID of every employee. If an employee does not have a corresponding department ID in the EmployeeDept DataFrame, return null for that employee. Return a DataFrame containing the columns id, name, and department_id. The result can be returned in any order. Pandas Schema Employees id: Unique ID of the employee (Primary key). name: Name of the employee. EmployeeDept id: Unique ID of the employee (Primary key). department_id: Department ID assigned to the employee.

title: Invalid Comments
description: Given a Pandas DataFrame comments containing the content of user comments, find the IDs of all invalid comments. A comment is considered invalid if the length of its content is strictly greater than 20 characters. Return a DataFrame containing the column comment_id. The result can be returned in any order. Pandas Schema comment_id: Unique ID of the comment (Primary key). content: Content of the comment. It consists of alphanumeric characters, spaces (' '), and exclamation marks ('!').

title: Salesperson Without Orders to Company "BLUE"
description: Given three Pandas DataFrames SalesPerson , Company, and Orders, find the names of all salespersons who did not have any orders associated with the company named "BLUE". Return a DataFrame containing the column name. The result can be returned in any order. Pandas Schema SalesPerson sales_id: Unique ID of the salesperson (Primary key). name: Name of the salesperson. salary: Salary of the salesperson. commission_rate: Commission rate of the salesperson. hire_date: Date when the salesperson was hired. Company com_id: Unique ID of the company (Primary key). name: Name of the company. city: City where the company is located. Orders order_id: Unique ID of the order (Primary key). com_id: Company ID corresponding to the order. sales_id: Salesperson ID corresponding to the order. order_date: Date on which the order was placed. amount: Amount of the order.
